screening_results.reason: The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal (Attend vs Reappraise) using visual stimuli (IAPS and alcohol images) in alcohol-dependent patients and matched healthy controls. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses with peak coordinates (MNI) and FWE-corrected inference, and the abstract and extracted data describe within-task effects (attend vs reappraise and emotional vs neutral) and group comparisons. All required elements for the meta-analysis are present: task fMRI, instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal), visual stimuli, eligible sample with control group, reported relevant task contrasts, and whole-brain coordinate results. No exclusion criteria from the list (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or reporting only between-group contrasts with no task effects) are met based on the document. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the reported task used an auditory stimulus (participants attempted to lower the volume), so the study does not meet I7 (visual emotional stimuli). While this is a task-based fMRI study (I5), reports a healthy sample (I8), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise peaks in standard space (I10) with acceptable reporting (I11), the reported analysis is a between-group parametric modulation with no within-group emotion-regulation contrast shown (E6 applies and I9 not met). Also, instructions do not describe an instructed emotion-regulation strategy like reappraisal (I6 not met). Therefore the study fails key inclusion criteria (I6, I7, I9) and meets exclusion E6.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I9 (reports a within-task emotion-related contrast: sch-evaluation > cc-evaluation), I10 (whole-brain results with peak coordinates, MNI), I11 (results reported in standard space). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy — participants rated agreement with statements, not instructed to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (stimuli are textual statements/words rather than visual images or film; the review excludes word/sentence-only stimuli), I8 (study reports only a patient sample with no separately reported control-group results). Exclusion criteria met: none of E3–E7 apply based on the document. Therefore the study does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria (notably I6 and I7) and is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; Negative Decrease vs Negative Look) (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS photographs (I7). Participant groups include patients and healthy controls, with within-group results reported separately for controls and MDD patients (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Negative Decrease > Negative Look and the reverse) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, with reported peak coordinates in Talairach and cluster-level correction across the whole brain (I10) and coordinates are reported in tables (I11). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task effects are reported. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I5 - it is a task-based fMRI study; I6 - it uses an instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal) task with arrows to increase/decrease/maintain; I7 - stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (negative and neutral); I8 - samples (young and older healthy adults) are eligible; I9 - reports within-task regulation contrasts (downregulate > maintain; upregulate > maintain) and unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral); I10 - reports whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space; I11 - results are reported in tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria apply (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects, and not an empathy/perspective-taking only study). Hence the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed a cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation strategy (I6) using visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample of adult participants is reported (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., decrease negative > look negative; look negative > look neutral) (I9). Crucially, at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates in MNI space is reported (Analysis 0, Table 1) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10) and the allowance for coordinate-table reporting (I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical design).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation (diminish/enhance) (I6) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) (I7). The sample includes PTSD patients and non-PTSD controls with results reported (I8). The paper reports regulation-related contrasts (e.g., diminish>maintain, enhance>maintain) (I9) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and peak tables (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain analyses are reported (not ROI-only), the results are task-evoked activation maps (not only connectivity), and within-group task effects are analyzed alongside between-group comparisons. Outcome: INCLUDED.

Study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) where participants were instructed to use emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal up- and down-regulation) during the task (I6). The regulated stimuli were visual (pictures of male and female proposers) (I7). Sample is reported (n=21 healthy adults) (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to regulation (e.g. Up > Look and Down > Look contrasts) (I9). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with FWE-corrected inference and peak coordinates in MNI space (I10), and these results are presented in tables (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-group task effects, and the paradigm involves instructed emotion regulation rather than unconstrained perspective-taking. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment in which participants were instructed to use emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal and expressive suppression) while viewing visual emotional stimuli (film clips and images). It includes within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > watch-negative; suppress > watch-negative) and an unregulated viewing contrast (watch-negative > watch-neutral). Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise with reported peak coordinates in Talairach space and cluster-level inference (AFNI AlphaSim), with peaks listed in tables. Sample (n=17 healthy adults) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based whole-brain fMRI (I5, I10), an instructed cognitive reappraisal emotion-regulation task (explicit instruction to reappraise; I6), visual stimuli (IAPS pictures; I7), healthy adult sample (I8), and reports task-related contrasts (e.g. RU–CU, PU–CU; reappraise/placebo vs control) with peak coordinates in standard space (Talairach) (I9, I11). NeuroStore lists multiple whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and coordinate tables and the abstract describes reappraisal and placebo activation differences, indicating within-task regulation effects were reported. No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are present (so not E4/E5), and within-task contrasts are reported (so not E6). Full text appears available via the extracted NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal/suppress blocks) (I6); uses visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) (I7); reports healthy adult participants (I8); includes within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Suppress > Maintain, Maintain > Suppress) (I9); and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results reported in MNI with peak coordinates (spatial scope whole brain, reported peaks) (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical (not E3), presents whole-brain analyses (not E4), is not limited to connectivity-only results (although it also reports ROI connectivity, whole-brain task maps are present, so not E5), reports within-group task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm (not E7). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS images with a within-subject emotion regulation manipulation (Reappraise vs Baseline, and Maintain vs Baseline). It reports group-level voxelwise results in MNI space with reported peak coordinates. All required inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI (I5); instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6); visual stimuli (I7); eligible sample reported (healthy adults) (I8); within-task regulation contrast reported (Reappraise > Baseline) (I9); whole-brain spatial scope and reported coordinates (I10) and results reported as peaks/tables acceptable (I11). No exclusion criteria are met: although inference used small-volume correction within an ROI, the analysis is marked whole-brain and reports standard-space peaks, so E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results) does not apply. Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that manipulates an antecedent-focused reappraisal-like strategy by presenting precedent descriptions (extrinsic/incidental reappraisal) to modulate emotional responses (I6). Stimuli are visual photographs (IAPS and others) (I7). Participants are healthy adults (I8). The paper reports within-task emotion-related contrasts (unpleasant > neutral within contexts) satisfying the requirement for an emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast (I9). Critically, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates are reported for real and fictitious contexts (whole-brain analyses with reported peaks), meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I10) and acceptable reporting of coordinate tables/peaks (I11). No exclusion criteria are met. The reported ROI results (amygdala, insula) are accompanied by whole-brain maps, so E4 does not apply.

The study reports a task-based fMRI emotion regulation paradigm with visual IAPS stimuli and explicit reappraisal instructions (meets I5, I6, I7). It provides whole-brain, cluster-corrected peak coordinates (meets I10 and I11) and the sample (late-life depressed patients) is an eligible participant group (meets I8). However, all reported analyses are omnibus between-group contrasts (remission status × scan time) with no within-task/regulation contrasts reported (e.g., reappraise > look) or any within-group task effects. Therefore it violates exclusion E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I9. Full text appears complete for screening.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed emotion regulation strategies (mindfulness vs cognitive reappraisal) during anticipation and perception (I6) using visual IAPS stimuli (I7) in a healthy sample (I8). Group-level, whole-brain analyses with peak coordinates in standard space (Talairach) are reported (I10) and tabulated (I11). However, all extracted contrasts are between-group interaction contrasts (mindfulness > cognitive control or vice versa) with no within-group emotion-regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look) or unregulated viewing contrast reported in the extraction. Therefore inclusion criterion I9 is not satisfied. Because the paper reports only between-group/interactions with no within-task effects for any group, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Full text appears complete in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal of anticipatory anxiety (I6). Regulation was applied during an anticipation/cue period signaled by visual countdowns, which satisfy the visual-stimulus requirement for this review (I7). The sample (healthy adults, n=15) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., regulation > control, regulation > anxiety) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space are reported (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), include within-group contrasts, and are not purely connectivity or non-empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study is a task-based fMRI cognitive reappraisal study using visual IAPS stimuli in healthy participants, so it meets I5, I6, I7, and I8. However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group interaction/group-comparison contrasts (HM > LM for down- and up-regulatory reappraisal) and does not report any within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look or down-regulate > maintain) or unregulated viewing contrasts for any group (failure to meet I9). Inference is reported as Small Volume Correction (pFWE) and the extracted analyses list SVC-only results/peaks, with no evidence of group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps or whole-brain inference (failure to meet I10). Therefore the study reports only between-group SVC results and no whole-brain or within-task effects, meeting exclusion criteria E6 and E4. Exclude on that basis.

Exclusion E6 applies: the NeuroStore record shows only between-group interaction contrasts (e.g. Controls Reappraise > UHR Attend; UHR View Negative > Controls View Neutral; Controls View Neutral > UHR Fixation) and no within-group task effects or simple unregulated viewing contrasts for any group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (sample includes patients and separately reported controls), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise results with peaks in MNI space), I11 (coordinates/tables clearly reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (the study does not report any within-task contrast or unregulated viewing contrast for a single group; only between-group interaction contrasts are reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E6.

This is a task-based fMRI study (n=76) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (detach/distancing vs permit), using visual stimuli (IAPS/EmoPicS). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Negative Detach Relaxation > Negative Permit Relaxation) and includes whole-brain, voxelwise (FWE-corrected) group-level analyses with reported MNI peaks. Although some ROI analyses are present (left amygdala), qualifying whole-brain results are also reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not non-empirical, not connectivity-only, not ROI-only, not between-group-only, and the perspective-taking instruction is used specifically to reduce emotional involvement as a regulation strategy). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs cognitive reappraisal (I5,I6). Emotional stimuli are visual (faces; I7). Sample is healthy adults with group results reported (n=26; I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraise > look (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in standard space (TAL) and whole-brain correction (I10); reporting in tables meets I11. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), within-group effects are present, and this is empirical fMRI activation (not connectivity-only or non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal) and a maintain condition (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). Participant groups include healthy controls and patient groups with results reported (I8). The report includes within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and unregulated viewing (Reappraise > Baseline; Maintain > Baseline) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with reported peak coordinates in Talairach space and cluster-corrected inference (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROI-only, connectivity-only, resting-state-only, or non-empirical designs, and within-task contrasts are reported. Although NeuroStore labels the contrasts as ‘omnibus, between-group’ in places, the presence of Reappraise>Baseline and Maintain>Baseline whole-brain contrasts with coordinates satisfies the meta-analysis requirements. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that explicitly instructs emotion regulation via causal attributions (internal vs external), using visual stimuli (faces). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. internal>view, external>view, internal>external) for both healthy controls and MDD patients, and provides whole-brain, cluster-corrected voxelwise results with peak coordinates. Both participant groups are reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not only ROI/SVC, not only connectivity/resting-state, not only between-group contrasts, not an empathy task without regulation). Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal (participants instructed to detach/think as an objective third party) using visual IAPS images (positive, negative, neutral). It reports within-task contrasts directly related to regulation (Reappraise > Experience; Experience > Reappraise) and an age-group interaction contrast. Analyses are whole-brain, cluster-corrected with reported peak coordinates in MNI space. Although PPI connectivity analyses are reported, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps are also provided. The sample includes healthy younger and older adults. Therefore it meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and does not trigger any exclusion criteria.

The study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review objective: it is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal: 'Decrease Neg') with visual stimuli (neutral and negative pictures). Within-task regulation contrasts are reported (Decrease Neg > Look Neg and its reverse) for groups separately. At least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis is reported with standard-space coordinates and FWE correction (analyses report whole-brain FWE-corrected results and peaks in MNI space). A control group’s results are reported separately. Although some reported contrasts used small-volume correction, whole-brain results are present, so exclusion for ROI-only results does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore include.

The study reports task-based fMRI of instructed emotion regulation (reappraisal to increase/decrease responses to angry faces) with visual stimuli (faces), healthy sample, and within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Decrease > Observe; Increase > Observe) at the group level. Spatial scope is whole-brain with coordinates in MNI and reported peak tables. Although the paper also reports resting-state seed-based connectivity, it additionally provides whole-brain task-evoked maps, so exclusion E5 does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal (reframe/ reinterpret to decrease negative emotion) using visual stimuli (72 static facial images from the NimStim set). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraise-Negative > Maintain-Negative; Maintain-Negative > Look-Neutral) at the group level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI (tables of peaks reported), and uses an appropriate GLM/random-effects model. Participants are healthy adults (n=21). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and the task involves instructed emotion regulation rather than mere perspective-taking. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs participants to use cognitive reappraisal to up- and down-regulate emotion (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is a healthy adult group reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., Increase > Look-Negative; Decrease > Look-Negative) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates and tables are provided (Talairach space) and inference is whole-brain corrected (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain activation maps and not only ROI or connectivity-only results. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study meets the meta-analysis requirements: it is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly investigates both emotion recognition and voluntary attentional regulation (the paper and record describe ‘voluntary attentional regulation’ and contrasts between emotion-evaluation and shape/orientation evaluation). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures. First-level SRT versus ERT contrasts were modeled and used in second-level (group) comparisons (independent-samples t-test of SRT vs ERT contrasts), and whole-brain, cluster-level FWE-corrected results with peak coordinates in MNI space are reported. Therefore it provides within-task contrasts related to regulation/viewing and whole-brain peak coordinates suitable for meta-analysis.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (BOLD) in which participants were instructed and trained to reduce negative emotion using cognitive reappraisal (Reduce vs Maintain). Stimuli were visual IAPS images. The paper reports a within-task regulation contrast (Reduce > Maintain) and whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (Talairach) and cluster-level correction. Participant groups (high-anxiety patients and healthy controls) are described and group-level results are reported separately. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy task). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study that instructed cognitive reappraisal (explicit downregulation) during presentation of visual IAPS images (emotion regulation task), with both Maintain and Reappraise conditions. The report includes within-task contrasts (Maintain > Reappraise and group interactions, pictures vs baseline) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates in MNI (tables of peaks referenced). A patient group (panic disorder) and healthy controls are reported separately. Although a seed PPI connectivity analysis is present, whole-brain activation maps are also reported (Table tbl2), so the study is not limited to ROI or connectivity-only results. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

The study meets several inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI; instructed emotion regulation using distraction and reappraisal; visual IAPS stimuli; healthy participant sample; and within-task contrasts such as reappraise > view and view negative > view neutral). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest analyses with small-volume correction (ROI SVC) and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps are reported. This violates inclusion criterion I10 and triggers exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results reported). Therefore the study is excluded.

Excluded because the NeuroStore record indicates only region-of-interest (ROI) results and only between-group interaction contrasts were reported. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only ROI results reported; no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported, with no within-group task effect reported). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—reappraisal and distraction), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups reported separately). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I9 (no within-task/regulation contrast for any group reported in this document) and I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Based on the provided document, the study must be excluded because it violates E4 and E6. Full text appears complete in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (self-distraction) during an anticipatory anxiety paradigm, reports within-task regulation contrasts and group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates. These meet inclusion criteria I5, I6, I8, I9, I10, and I11. However, the regulated stimuli are auditory cues (high/low pitch beeps) and painful electrical stimulation rather than visual stimuli; therefore inclusion criterion I7 (emotional stimuli are VISUAL) is NOT met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because it fails I7, the study is excluded from this meta-analysis.

The paper reports a task-based fMRI study instructing cognitive reappraisal (regulate vs view) of visual IAPS images in healthy participants (n=14). It includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (Reappraisal>View and View>Reappraisal) with FDR correction and reported peak coordinates in Talairach space, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task activation maps. The study also reports seed-based connectivity, but this is accompanied by the required whole-brain activation results. No exclusion criteria are met. Note: the NeuroStore tag ‘between-group’ on the Reappraisal>View entry is likely a metadata label; the entry specifies a group GLM random-effects analysis of the task contrast and lists whole-brain corrected peaks, which fulfils the within-task contrast requirement.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using visual stimuli (faces) with a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (faces > shapes) and reports whole-brain group-level results and coordinates; participants are healthy adults. However, the task did not instruct participants to use any emotion regulation strategy (instructions: match faces/shapes; explicitly 'no instructions to regulate emotion'). Although the paper reports correlations with trait ERQ reappraisal scores, this is observational (cross-subject regression) and not an instructed regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > look). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) of emotional responses to visual stimuli (IAPS and spider pictures). Within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing are reported (e.g. up/down vs look; spider vs aversive), and several analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps reported in MNI with peak coordinates and cluster inference. The sample is a clinical group (spider phobics) with within-group results presented. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task effects are reported. Therefore it meets all relevant inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli in an eligible sample (children and adults), the NeuroStore record reports only seed-based/effective connectivity analyses (Granger) and provides no clear within-task contrasts of instructed emotion regulation (e.g., reappraise > look, down-regulate > maintain) or an explicit whole-brain task-evoked activation map. The task appears to be an emotional Go/No-Go (response inhibition) paradigm rather than an instructed cognitive reappraisal or other explicit emotion-regulation instruction. Therefore the study does not meet the requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation task (I6) nor the requirement for a within-task regulation contrast (I9) or clearly reported whole-brain activation results (I10). Exclusion E5 applies because only connectivity results are reported without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps.

Excluded because the paper reports ONLY between-group interaction contrasts and does not present any within-group task activation maps. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli—IAPS images), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups reported), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported; MNI coordinates), I11 (results reported as peak coordinate tables). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task contrasts for regulation or unregulated viewing reported in the document; NeuroStore extracts only between-group interaction contrasts). Full text appears complete per the provided record.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment where participants were instructed to use cognitive reappraisal (up- and down-regulation) while viewing visual stimuli (photographs of proposers) during a Dictator Game. The NeuroStore record reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., up > look, down > look, up > down) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference and MNI peak coordinates. Participant sample is healthy and acceptable. All required inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with instructed emotion regulation strategies (Detachment, Reinterpretation, Distraction, Expressive Suppression) using visual IAPS pictures; reports within-task contrasts (multiple ‘Regulate Negative > Permit Negative’ and Permit > Regulate contrasts) and valence contrasts; group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected peak coordinates in MNI space; sample reported (healthy participants, n=74, and subgroup within-group analyses). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains within-group task effects).

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI experiment with instructed emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and distraction) applied during stimulus presentation (I5,I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample is healthy adults and thus eligible (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and viewing (e.g., reappraisal > view, distraction > view, view emotional > neutral) (I9). Results include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in MNI space and tables of reported peaks (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain activations (not only ROI or connectivity; so not E4/E5), includes within-group task effects (not only between-group; not E6), and involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking without regulation (not E7).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (distancing/perspective-taking reappraisal; I6), uses visual emotional stimuli (60 IAPS pictures; I7), includes an eligible sample of healthy participants (I8), reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., regulation > no regulation, negative > neutral; I9), and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with peak coordinates in MNI space (several analyses report whole-brain FWE-corrected results and tables of peaks; I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are triggered: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), within-group task effects are present, and the task is explicit emotion regulation rather than mere perspective-taking without regulation. Thus the paper should be INCLUDED in the review.

Exclusion reasons: E4 (only region-of-interest / small-volume-corrected results reported; no whole-brain voxelwise analyses extracted) and E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effects reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reappraisal and distraction), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures), I8 (eligible sample). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I9 (no clear within-task contrast reported for any group; extracted contrasts are interactions/between-group), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation maps or coordinates reported; spatial scope is ROI). Full text is available in NeuroStore extraction, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: an emotion-regulation strategy was not instructed. The task manipulated preceding descriptions (neutral/positive vs negative) producing implicit reappraisal, but participants were instructed to passively view and rate valence rather than to deliberately reappraise or otherwise regulate. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — IAPS images), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports a within-task contrast related to emotion regulation: NNEG-DES > NEG-DES), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates in MNI), I11 (results reported as coordinate table). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 violations). Full text was available in the record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

All inclusion criteria are met: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal/distancing) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli were visual (negative and neutral pictures) (I7). Sample is healthy participants with n=108 (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (WatchNeg > RegulateNeg and RegulateNeg > WatchNeg) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are provided with peaks in MNI space and reported peaks (analysis_1 reports uncorrected whole-brain peak-level results; analysis_0 includes SVC but does not negate the presence of whole-brain results) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10,I11). The study addresses the review objective and reports task-based fMRI of instructed cognitive reappraisal to visual stimuli in healthy children, with within-task contrasts (reappraise > view sad; view sad > neutral) and group-level whole-brain analyses. The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed emotion regulation (self-focused reappraisal to increase/decrease; I6) with visual stimuli (static angry and neutral faces; I7). This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based BOLD fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion regulation strategy (Decrease = reinterpretation; I6) with visual stimuli (IAPS images; I7). The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (reduce vs. maintain) using visual stimuli (Native Chinese Affective Picture System). This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal as the emotion regulation strategy (I6) using visual IAPS images (I7). This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. Excluded under E6. This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (distancing: “Far” vs “Close”) qualifying as cognitive reappraisal/perspective-taking (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample includes PMDD patients and healthy controls with results reported (I8). Analyses include an explicit regulation contrast (far, negative > close, negative), a within-subject analysis (interaction across menstrual phases) satisfying the requirement for a within-task regulation contrast (I9). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-task effects are reported (E4–E6 not met).

This is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (analyze/reappraise), an eligible clinical sample (MDD), within-task regulation contrasts, and whole-brain voxelwise results reported in MNI coordinates. However, the regulated stimuli are autobiographical memory cue phrases that prompt internally generated recall (textual/script-driven imagery) rather than externally presented visual stimuli (images or videos). That fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded because it does not meet I7 (stimuli visual).

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli and whole-brain, coordinate-reported results (meets I5, I7, I8, I10). There is also no instruction to perform an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/distancing/acceptance). Because the paper reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect, it meets exclusion criterion E6 and therefore must be excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation task that explicitly includes cognitive reappraisal (reinterpret negative images to reduce negative response) (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample (healthy female participants) is acceptable and reported separately (I8). Reported contrasts include both regulation (Reappraise Negative > Attend Negative) and unregulated viewing (View Negative > View Neutral) within-group (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, FWE-corrected group-level maps with reported peak coordinates (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical paper, or empathy-without-regulation issues). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the report provides only between-group contrasts/interactions relating to regulation and does not present any within-task regulation contrast (e.g., reappraise > attend) or an unregulated viewing contrast for either group. Exclusion ID met: E6. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation — reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample includes patients and controls reported separately), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with reported peaks), I11 (results reported in standard space). Inclusion ID not met: I9 (no within-task regulation contrast or unregulated viewing contrast reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E6.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps, violating inclusion criterion I10 and meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain evidence reported; shared spatial scope across analyses = region of interest). Therefore EXCLUDED.

Exclusion E6 applies: the NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction maps and seed-based PPI connectivity results, with no within-group task contrast (e.g., reappraise > maintain) reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation—Reduce vs Maintain), I7 (visual stimuli—negative images), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups reported separately), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analysis reported), I11 (whole-brain results described). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation for any group is reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E6.

This fMRI study uses a task-based emotion regulation paradigm (cognitive reappraisal) with visual stimuli (neutral and negative images) and reports within-subject, task-related whole-brain voxelwise results. The provided analysis is a within-group parametric modulation of stimulus intensity during reappraisal (association), reported in MNI coordinates with cluster-level thresholding, satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain group-level activation map. Sample characteristics are reported (n=30, mean age 21.97). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using visual emotional stimuli (composite face/scene pictures) with an instructed appraisal condition (like/dislike) contrasted against implicit emotion processing, which fits the review objective of regulation vs. unregulated viewing. It reports within-task contrasts (e.g., appraisal > implicit) and whole-brain, voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates and FWE-corrected maps. Sample (n=31 healthy adults) and analyses meet participant and reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain activation maps are reported (not only ROI or connectivity), and there are within-task effects. Therefore the study should be included.

The NeuroStore record documents a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructed emotion regulation (INCREASE, DECREASE, LOOK) using cognitive reappraisal (self- and situation-focused). Stimuli were visual (27 IAPS images). Reported within-task contrasts include reappraisal vs look (e.g., Increase Negative > Look Negative; Look Negative > Decrease Negative), satisfying the required regulation contrasts. Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise with peak coordinates in MNI reported (tables of peaks listed). Participants (n=24) and a GLM/regression model are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not empathy-only). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I11.

The study reports a task-based fMRI emotion regulation experiment with visual IAPS stimuli and instructed reappraisal, and provides whole-brain group analyses. However, the only extracted analysis is a between-group interaction contrast (GDPs regulate > HCs experience) with no within-task regulation contrast (e.g. reappraise > look) reported for any group. The review requires at least one within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast (I9). Because only between-group/interactions are reported, this meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I9. Full text appears complete for screening.

This is an event-related, task-based fMRI study (I5) using the Cued Emotional Conflict Task which instructs participants to inhibit a dominant response to emotional faces (an instructed cognitive control of emotional response), meeting the emotion-regulation instruction criterion (I6). Stimuli are visual static faces from KDEF (I7). Sample is healthy participants reported with demographics (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation/inhibition (e.g., opposite > actual; opposite-sad vs opposite-happy) and cross-subject regressions with reappraisal scores (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise with FDR correction and peak coordinates in MNI space (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are present (not ROI-only), not only connectivity or between-group-only contrasts, and it is empirical data. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment instructing an emotion-regulation strategy (“reality checking”) during viewing of visual negative IAPS pictures, with healthy participants. It reports within-task regulation contrasts for both Feedback and Control groups (e.g. regulate > view within-group contrasts) and between-group interactions, analyzed with group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLMs and corrected voxelwise/cluster inference; peak coordinates are reported in Talairach. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11). No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task effects are reported). fulltext is complete for screening purposes.

Excluded because the study does not address task-based emotion regulation of visual stimuli required for the review. Therefore the study does not satisfy the review’s core inclusion criteria and is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using visual stimuli (video clips) and reports a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (risk-taking > safe) at the whole-brain group level with MNI peak coordinates (Table of 17 peaks). However, participants were instructed only to observe the videos (no emotion-regulation strategy was instructed), so it does not meet inclusion criterion I6. No exclusion criteria are triggered (E3, E4, E5, E6, E7 do not apply). Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to meet all required inclusion criteria (specifically I6).

This study uses a task-based fMRI cognitive reappraisal paradigm with visual stimuli in a sample including MDD and healthy children and reports within-task contrasts (via PPI). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample with patient and control groups), and I9 (within-task regulation-related contrasts). However, all reported results are seed-based PPI (functional connectivity) analyses; no group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (voxelwise activation contrasts with peak coordinates) are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E5 (reports only seed-based connectivity without an accompanying whole-brain task activation map). Conclusion: EXCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion regulation task with a Reduce instruction to minimize emotional response (cognitive reappraisal/related strategy) and a Maintain condition (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). Sample includes adolescents with MDD and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts (Maintain > Reduce) for each group (I9). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation analyses are reported with peak coordinates in Talairach–Tournoux space (I10), and coordinates are presented in tables (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, reports whole-brain task activation (not only ROI or connectivity), and includes within-group task effects. Therefore it should be included in the meta-analysis.

The study uses a task-based fMRI emotion regulation paradigm with instructed cognitive reappraisal of visual (video) stimuli and reports patient and control groups (I5, I6, I7, I8 satisfied). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI)-based between-group contrasts (e.g., HC > SAD) with FDR correction within ROIs; no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps or peak coordinates from whole-brain analyses are reported. Additionally, the NeuroStore extractions list only between-group contrasts and do not report any within-task (e.g., reappraise > watch) task effect for either group. Therefore the study fails to meet I9 and I10 and meets exclusion criteria E4 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (only between-group contrasts reported, no within-group task effects). Excluded for not providing whole-brain task activation results and lacking within-task contrasts required by the review.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed cognitive reappraisal to regulate emotion (I6). The stimuli are visual static pictures (IAPS and internet photos) (I7). The sample includes unmedicated MDD patients and healthy controls with group-wise analyses reported (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. negative/real > negative/photo and omnibus reappraisal effects) (I9). Crucially, multiple analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps reported in standard MNI space with peak coordinates (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are present (not ROI-only), task activation contrasts are reported (not only between-group interactions), and this is empirical fMRI data. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (first-person engagement/up-regulation of positive-social emotions) using visual stimuli (112 positive-social and 112 neutral photographs from IAPS, NAPS, GAPED). Participants are healthy (n=23). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., regulation > viewing; positive > neutral). At least some analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in MNI and reported peaks (positive > neutral analyses report whole-brain FWE-corrected voxel-level results and peaks). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I5–I11 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (not exclusively ROI/SVC, not only connectivity, not non-empirical, contains within-group effects, and involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking).

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based BOLD fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal during trials (I6), uses visual stimuli (adolescent face images) (I7), includes adolescent patient and healthy control groups reported separately (I8), reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (reappraisal > attend) (I9), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (I10/I11). The document also shows GLM task activation results (analysis 25533974_analysis_0) and PPI connectivity analyses, but the presence of whole-brain task activation satisfies the requirement and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Therefore the paper should be included.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with instructed emotion regulation (expressive suppression and imitation as regulation strategies) to visual stimuli (dynamic facial videos), healthy sample reported, within-task contrasts directly addressing regulation (eSUP > GENDER; eSUP > IMITATION; IMT contrasts), and group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported MNI peak coordinates. Reporting is adequate (tables of peaks). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, between-group-only, or empathy-without-regulation) are met. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of instructed emotion regulation to visual stimuli.

Exclusion E4 applies: the NeuroStore extraction shows only a region-of-interest analysis (Spatial scope: region of interest; inference: corrected within ROI; amygdala bilaterally). No group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map or peak coordinates in standard space are reported in the extracted analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation - cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli - IAPS pictures), I8 (eligible sample - healthy adults), I9 (within-task regulation contrast reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level analysis reported). Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal: Regulate vs Attend), using visual stimuli (colored cues and a picture of a cigarette pack). It reports a within-task regulation contrast (Regulate CS+ > Attend CS+) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference and peak coordinates in Talairach space. The sample (nicotine-dependent smokers) is an eligible participant group. No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-group task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only paradigm). Therefore it meets all relevant inclusion criteria for the review.

This study meets all inclusion criteria relevant to the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed emotion regulation strategies (increase/decrease via reappraisal/distancing; I6) with visual stimuli (IAPS images; I7). The sample includes clinical groups (BD and Sz) and healthy controls with results reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. increase>maintain; decrease>maintain; I9). Results are whole-brain, voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster-level corrected inference (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain activations rather than ROI-only results (not E4), is not limited to connectivity-only analyses (not E5), includes within-group task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions (not E7).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual stimuli (IAPS images) with within-subject decrease/increase/maintain instructions. It reports multiple within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (e.g., increase>maintain, decrease>increase, maintain>decrease) at the group second-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in standard spaces (MNI and Talairach) and tables of reported peaks. Sample is healthy adults (n=18). All inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The fMRI session and reported whole-brain contrasts concern a placebo analgesia pain task with thermal (noxious) stimuli, not an instructed emotion-regulation task using visual emotional stimuli. While the paper includes a separate cognitive reappraisal ability (CRA) task using pictures (behavioral) and uses ERQ/CRA scores as covariates, there is no within-scanner, within-task contrast of instructed emotion regulation (e.g. reappraise > view) on visual stimuli. Therefore the study does not meet the core inclusion requirements for this meta-analysis (an fMRI task instructing emotion regulation of visual stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

Study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It is a task-based fMRI study that instructed emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and expressive suppression) and included a viewing condition. Stimuli are visual (Chinese Affective Picture System images). Participants are healthy adults (n=47). The document reports within-task contrasts including an unregulated viewing contrast (watch-negative > watch-neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps with peaks in MNI space (FWE-corrected), satisfying whole-brain evidence. Although the study also reports seed-based PPI connectivity, whole-brain task activation results are present, so the study is not excluded under E5. Full text is available in the provided record.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (socially induced reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli are visual (IAPS aversive pictures and video clips) (I7). The sample is healthy adult participants with results reported for the group (n=19) (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. Reg>Look, Social-Reg>Social-Look) (I9). Analyses are group-level whole-brain voxelwise with coordinates in MNI and reported peak tables (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and the task involves explicit regulation instructions rather than mere perspective-taking. Therefore the article should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructed participants to apply emotion regulation strategies (cognitive reappraisal, suppression, up-regulation) while viewing visual stimuli (palatable food pictures). It reports within-subject, within-task contrasts (main effect of cognitive control strategy; omnibus within-group F-test) and a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise RFX ANOVA with results in Talairach space and 23 reported peak coordinates. Sample (n=14 healthy adults) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-task effects). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

All required inclusion criteria are met: this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (permit/acceptance) vs viewing (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is healthy participants reported with demographics (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts both for regulation and unregulated viewing (permit > view, view negative > view neutral) (I9). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in MNI reported (tables) (I10,I11). Although results used small-volume correction within ROIs, the spatial scope is listed as whole brain and peak coordinates are provided, so this does not trigger exclusion for ROI-only reporting. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This paper meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal (DECREASE vs LOOK) as the emotion regulation strategy (I6). The stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7). The sample is a healthy adult group reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (decrease-negative > look-negative) and an unregulated viewing contrast (look-negative > look-neutral) (I9). Multiple analyses are reported as group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain results in addition to ROI analyses (not E4), does not report only connectivity/resting-state analyses (not E5), does not report only between-group contrasts without within-task effects (not E6), and it is not a pure perspective-taking/empathy task without regulation instructions (not E7). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an explicit, instructed emotion-regulation fMRI task using cognitive reappraisal (I6) with visual IAPS stimuli (I7) in healthy participants (I8). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5). It includes within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. increase/decrease > maintain; up-regulating > maintain) (I9). Importantly, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates are provided (Analyses 30455624_analysis_0 and _3), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement (I10/I11). Although some results are ROI-based (dorsomedial PFC), whole-brain results are also reported, so exclusion for ROI-only reporting does not apply. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the review.

The study meets several inclusion criteria (task-based fMRI; instructed emotion regulation with increase/decrease strategies; visual stimuli (IAPS and in-house images); eligible sample including ASD and TD controls; and reports condition contrasts such as 'Decrease versus look' and 'Increase versus look'). However, all reported analyses in the NeuroStore record are region-of-interest (ROI) scoped, and no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) activation maps or peak coordinates in a standard space are reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I10 and violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Excluded for E4.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed cognitive reappraisal using visual IAPS pictures with auditory Increase/Maintain/Decrease instructions. The study reports within-subject regulation contrasts (Increase>Maintain, Decrease>Maintain, Increase>Decrease) and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported in MNI space with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected inference. All required inclusion criteria (I5-I11) are satisfied; no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion based on non-visual script stimuli and ROI-only reporting. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (study reports results within regions-of-interest with FWE correction within ROIs and no indication of a whole-brain voxelwise task activation map) and E6 (the provided analyses list only between-group interaction contrasts; no within-group/regulation > maintain contrasts are reported in the document). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy — reappraisal/distancing — was used), I8 (sample acceptable: clinical and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli are script-driven sentences — non-visual — so do not meet the visual-stimuli requirement), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast reported in the extraction; only between-group contrasts are shown), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise peak coordinates are reported; spatial scope is ROI). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal (distancing) as an emotion regulation strategy (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual (abstract reward cues and monetary feedback displays), satisfying the visual-stimulus requirement (I7). The sample (n=16 healthy adults) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Distance vs Permit; EV × strategy interactions), meeting I9. Importantly, a group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrast (Distance vs Permit) is reported (analysis 8: whole-brain, p<0.001 cluster extent), satisfying I10; reporting in the NeuroStore record is clear (I11). Although several ROI/SVC results are reported, whole-brain results are also provided, so no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria.

The NeuroStore record indicates this is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation using visual stimuli (I5, I6, I7). Participants are healthy and reported (I8), and the paper reports within-task contrasts showing decreased amygdala activation during regulation versus emotion conditions (I9). However, all reported analyses in the record are restricted to a priori regions of interest (amygdala, IFG) and the connectivity PPI is ROI-scoped with inference corrected within ROI. There is no clear evidence in the document of a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). Therefore the study reports only ROI/SVC (and ROI-based connectivity) results and meets exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9. Inclusion criterion not met: I10. Exclusion criterion met: E4.

This event-related task-based fMRI study instructs cognitive regulation (reappraisal/suppression) of responses to visual food images in adolescents and reports within-task contrasts contrasting regulation vs imagine/view conditions. Results are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates (Table t2) in MNI space and corrected whole-brain inference. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria for emotion regulation of visual stimuli and provides usable whole-brain coordinates for meta-analysis.

The study is excluded because the regulated stimuli are written negative self-belief sentences (word stimuli), not visual images or video, so it fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: breath- and distraction-focused attention), I8 (sample: clinical patient group acceptable), I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts, e.g., Breath > React), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore exclusion is based on failure to meet I7 (stimulus modality).

Exclusion: E4 and E5 are met because the NeuroStore record reports only ROI-based, small-volume-corrected and seed-based connectivity (gPPI) results (midbrain ROI with SVC; left vlPFC seed) and does not report any group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive regulation: Distance vs Attend), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures), I8 (sample: healthy participants reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrast Distance > Attend). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation map with peak coordinates reported in this document). Therefore the study must be excluded under E4/E5.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment using instructed emotion regulation (participants were instructed to experience and increase tenderness or anguish via real-time neurofeedback), satisfying the core requirement of instructed regulation. The stimuli include a first-person virtual environment (visual) with accompanying music, so visual emotional stimuli are present. Sample is healthy participants. The report contains within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Tenderness > Anguish and Anguish > Tenderness), including within-group contrasts at each site, and also whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (Analyses 5 and 6 report whole-brain FWE-corrected maps). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria are met (the paper reports whole-brain analyses in addition to ROI/SVC results). Note: there is some ambiguity because primary contrasts compare two regulated emotion states rather than regulate vs. passive view, hence confidence is slightly reduced, but the study nevertheless involves instructed regulation of visual emotional stimuli and provides whole-brain activation coordinates.

The study uses a film-based emotion regulation fMRI task with instructed reappraisal and visual stimuli, but the NeuroStore record reports only seed-based PPI connectivity results (right amygdala) as a between-group interaction; no within-group task activation contrasts or whole-brain task-evoked activation maps are provided. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E5 (only seed-based/effective connectivity reported without a whole-brain task activation map) and E6 (reports only between-group interaction with no within-group task effects). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation/reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli — film clips), I8 (sample acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task contrast for regulation within a group reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (detachment, a form of cognitive reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli are visual static pictures (negative, neutral, positive) (I7). Sample includes anorexia nervosa patients and an age-matched healthy control group with results reported for group contrasts and main effects (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation and viewing contrasts (e.g., negative watch > negative distance; negative distance > negative watch; negative watch > neutral) (I9). Results are whole-brain, voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in MNI space (I10) and are clearly described (I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or empathy-without-regulation paradigms).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructed cognitive emotion regulation (distancing/reappraisal instructions) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli were visual IAPS pictures (I7). The sample comprised healthy participants reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts and regressions related to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g., regulated > non-regulated effects, subsequent memory effects) (I9). Multiple analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates in MNI space and results reported in tables (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: it is empirical fMRI activation work (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or empathy-without-regulation). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria were violated.

The study reports task-based fMRI (I5) with an instructed emotion-regulation task (increase/decrease causal-attribution strategy) meeting I6. Stimuli are visual static facial images (I7). Sample includes patients and healthy controls with group-level results reported (I8). The paper reports regulation-related contrasts (Regulation > View; Regulation Happy > View Happy; Regulation Sad > View Sad) satisfying I9. All regulation analyses are whole-brain, cluster-corrected with reported peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space (I10,I11). NeuroStore lists peak tables (Tables 5) and whole-brain AFNI 3dClustSim correction, so results are suitable for meta-analysis. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (reappraisal and expressive suppression) during viewing of visual stimuli (IAPS and other photographic scenes), satisfying I5–I7. Participants are healthy humans (n=19), satisfying I8. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., REAP>ESUP, ESUP>REAP, and natural viewing contrasts), satisfying I9. Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space are reported (several analyses explicitly labeled 'whole brain' with reported peaks/tables), satisfying I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results are present, not ROI-only; within-group contrasts reported). Full text appears available in the provided record.

The report describes a Go/No-Go frustration task with visual stimuli and whole-brain peak coordinates, but the paper does not report any instructed emotion-regulation condition (no cognitive reappraisal or other regulation instructions) and the extracted analyses are all between-group interaction contrasts (patients vs controls). Thus it appears only between-group contrasts are reported with no within-group regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts. Exclusion criteria E6 applies. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation), I9 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported). Therefore the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (n=24 healthy adults) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (distance/reappraisal vs permit) during anticipation of monetary rewards. Stimuli are visual reward cues (€1.00 and €0.05); regulation is explicitly instructed. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. Regulate > Permit) and interactions, and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected peaks (reported in tables). These satisfy the review’s requirements for task fMRI, instructed cognitive reappraisal/distancing, visual stimuli, within-task regulation contrasts, and whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only connectivity, not non-empirical).

This study meets the review objective as an fMRI task where participants view visual emotional stimuli (violent vs non-violent game play) without instructed regulation. Criteria met: I5 (task-based event-related fMRI during gameplay), I7 (visual stimuli: video game), I8 (healthy sample, n=38), I9 (reports within-task contrasts relevant to unregulated viewing: violent action > non-violent action and inverse), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in Talairach), I11 (results reported in tables/figures). Although I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not satisfied, the meta-analysis objective allows inclusion of unregulated viewing contrasts per I9. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: whole-brain analyses are reported (not ROI-only), there are within-group task effects, and this is empirical task-based activation (not connectivity-only). Statistical inference is whole-brain corrected and peaks are provided, so the study supplies suitable coordinates for meta-analysis. Therefore include.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation task (affect labeling vs gender labeling), which qualifies as an instructed regulation strategy (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual (photographs of faces; I7). The sample includes both SAD patients and healthy controls with group results reported (I8). Multiple analyses report within-task regulation contrasts (affect label > gender label) and pre/post regulation contrasts (I9). Several analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise, corrected and report peak coordinates (I10,I11). Although the paper includes seed-based (gPPI) connectivity analyses, it also reports task-evoked BOLD activation (analysis_0), so it does not meet exclusion E5 or E4. No exclusion criteria (E3, E4, E5, E6, E7) apply. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis and none of the exclusion criteria.

Excluded because study does not test an emotion-regulation task with visual stimuli and reports only a between-group interaction. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample: clinical older adults with MCI and controls reported), I10 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise map with peak coordinates in MNI reported). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; task was resting with eyes open), I7 (no emotional VISUAL stimuli; task was rest), I9 (no within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation or unregulated viewing reported). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) using visual stimuli (I7) with a sample including patients and controls (I8). It reports an unregulated viewing contrast (negative > neutral pictures) (I9) and provides whole-brain peak coordinates in standard space (I10,I11). However, the task does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal or other instructed regulation); instead it examines the effect of painful stimulation on affect and reports primarily PPI connectivity analyses. Therefore it fails to meet I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation task) and must be excluded per the inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (distraction; I6) with visual stimuli (IAPS pictures; I7). It includes a clinical sample with trauma-exposed controls reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (distraction > passive viewing; I9) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (I10,I11). Although inference used small-volume correction within predefined ROIs, the NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain spatial scope and reports peak coordinates, so no exclusion criterion for ROI-only reporting (E4) is triggered. The study also includes connectivity analyses but also reports task activation contrasts. Therefore it should be included in the meta-analysis of instructed visual emotion regulation.

This study instructs participants to increase/decrease emotional responses to errors during a cognitive task, and reports within-task contrasts of regulation (e.g. increase>decrease) and whole-brain results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instruction to regulate emotion), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task emotion-regulation contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), I11 (whole-brain results reported in tables). However, the regulated stimuli are not visual emotional stimuli: regulation is applied to the participant’s emotional response to making errors on a neutral visual letter task (internal/event-related), rather than to emotional visual stimuli (e.g., IAPS images, emotional faces, or film clips). Therefore I7 (emotional stimuli are visual) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because I7 is not satisfied, the study does not match the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded.

This fMRI study instructs participants to up- and downregulate emotional responses using reappraisal strategies while viewing visual (IAPS) threat-related pictures, with simultaneous behavioral and physiological measures. It reports within-task contrasts (increase > view, decrease > view, increase > decrease, etc.) at the group level. Crucially, several analyses are whole-brain, random-effects, voxelwise maps with corrected inference reported (increase-minus-view and decrease-minus-view whole-brain analyses), and peak coordinates are provided in MNI space. All inclusion criteria are met (I5: task-based fMRI; I6: instructed emotion regulation/reappraisal; I7: visual stimuli; I8: sample acceptable; I9: within-task regulation contrasts reported; I10: at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise map reported; I11: coordinates/tables provided). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This study should be excluded because it does not instruct participants to regulate their emotional responses and does not report any emotion-regulation contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli—faces), I8 (sample acceptable—healthy adults), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in standard space), I11 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—task is Go/No-Go with response inhibition, not regulation/reappraisal), I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation such as reappraise>look or down-regulate>maintain). No exclusion criteria from the review are triggered (E3–E7 not applicable). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion-labeling task (implicit/affective labeling) that functions as an instructed emotion regulation strategy (I6). Stimuli are visual (NimStim face photographs) (I7). Sample includes adolescents (I8). The reported analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (labeling > matching) and interaction contrasts (I9). Whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and appropriate cluster correction (I10); results are presented in standard reportable form (I11).
