No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain analyses are present (not ROI-only, E4 not met), task activation maps are reported (E5 not met), within-task contrasts exist (E6 not met), and the task is not an empathy/perspective-taking paradigm without regulation instructions (E7 not met).

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal; down-regulate the emotional response) (I6). The emotional stimuli were visual (colour photographs from the Karolinska Directed Emotional Faces set) (I7). Sample: healthy adults (n=18) reported (I8). The paper reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (reappraise > rate; down-regulate > rate) (I9). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise random-effects maps with reported peak coordinates and voxelwise thresholds (I10), and results are presented in tables/analyses as extracted (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: this is empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and involves instructed reappraisal rather than perspective-taking without emotion regulation. Therefore INCLUDE.

The study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses (Amygdala, Insula, ACC, vmPFC, dLPFC) with results corrected within ROIs and does not report any whole-brain voxelwise group-level activation maps. All reported contrasts are between-group interactions (controls vs relatives) of emotion-viewing contrasts, with no within-group task activation maps shown in the NeuroStore extract. Therefore it violates E4 (ONLY ROI results) and E6 (ONLY between-group contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli - photographs of faces), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts: negative vs happy). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates), I11 (no whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Based on these, the study must be excluded.

Excluded because the report contains only region-of-interest (ROI) results and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (exclusion E4). The study nevertheless meets several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS and images), I8 (sample reported), and I9 (within-task regulation contrasts: view>regulate for negative and positive). It does NOT meet I10 (no whole-brain/voxelwise results with standard-space peak coordinates; spatial scope is ROI). Full text appears complete for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This is a task-based fMRI study that instructs emotion regulation strategies (implementation intentions and goal intention reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (implementation intention > attend; goal intention > attend) and interaction contrasts, all at the group level with whole-brain, voxelwise inference (Talairach coordinates) and peak tables. Sample is healthy adults. Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply (not non-empirical; not ROI-only; includes task activation maps in addition to connectivity; contains within-group contrasts; not an empathy-only task).

The study meets inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reality checking), I7 (visual stimuli: negative emotional faces), I8 (healthy adult sample, n=6), and I9 (reports within-task contrasts: view > regulate and omnibus within-group effects). However, it does NOT provide a group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation map: all reported analyses use region-of-interest/region-level inference (right and left amygdala, anatomically or functionally defined). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only ROI results reported, no whole-brain analysis). Although coordinates and peaks are reported, they arise from ROI/region-level analyses rather than a whole-brain voxelwise group map, so I10 is not satisfied. Conclusion: exclude for failing I10 and meeting E4.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal) and also includes an unregulated passive viewing condition and a placebo manipulation. Stimuli are visual (IAPS and newly developed pictures). Participants are healthy adults (n=45). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., Reappraisal > Passive Viewing; Reappraisal > Placebo; Passive Viewing > Placebo). NeuroStore extraction indicates whole-brain spatial scope with reported peak coordinates in MNI space (tables), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps; although some inferences used small-volume correction, the presence of whole-brain scope and coordinate tables means results are not limited to ROI-only reporting. The study also contains connectivity analyses but not exclusively. Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and no exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (I7; IAPS) with separate patient and control groups reported (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts of unregulated anticipation/viewing (e.g. expectation negative > neutral; exp.neg > exp.neut) satisfying the requirement for an unregulated viewing contrast (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster-level inference reported (I10, I11). Although no instructed regulation (reappraisal) was used (I6 not met), the meta-analysis objective accepts studies that include unregulated viewing contrasts, so inclusion is appropriate. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, or non-empirical paper).

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) in which an emotion regulation strategy was explicitly instructed (Enhance vs Watch; up-regulation) fulfilling I6. Stimuli were visual static images from EmoPicS (I7). Sample is a healthy participant cohort (n=63) meeting I8. The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., PosUp > PosWatch, NeuUp > NeuWatch, Up > Watch) satisfying I9. Several analyses are reported as whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with MNI coordinates and peak tables (Analyses 6,7,8,9), meeting I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain results (not only ROI, so not E4), is not only connectivity (not E5), includes within-group contrasts (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation instructions (not E7). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none, so it should be INCLUDED in the review.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (increase/decrease/attend) using visual IAPS pictures and an acceptable sample (I5, I6, I7, I8 satisfied). However, the only extracted reported analysis is a region-of-interest, between-group interaction contrast (insecure > secure for increase vs attend). The document does not report any within-group/regulation contrast (e.g., increase > attend within a group) nor any whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps. Therefore the study fails inclusion criteria I9 and I10 and meets exclusion criteria E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions) and E4 (reports only ROI results with no whole-brain analysis). Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation task (reappraise vs attend/view) (I6); visual stimuli (IAPS images) (I7); includes clinical (GAD) and healthy control groups reported separately (I8); reports within-task effects relevant to regulation (Main effect of Condition and Group × Condition interaction) (I9); whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster-corrected inference (I10); reporting via tables of peaks (I11). No exclusion criteria are met. The NeuroStore record includes sufficient methodological detail (task, model, corrections) to confirm eligibility.

The NeuroStore record documents a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (Reappraise > Maintain) using visual stimuli (IAPS negative scenes). It reports a within-task emotion-regulation contrast (Reappraise > Maintain) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference (Talairach coordinates; Monte Carlo cluster correction), and peak coordinates are provided. Sample (n=51 healthy adults) and design are appropriate. Thus the study meets I5-I11. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs/SVC (E4), not only connectivity (E5), not only between-group contrasts (E6), and not an empathy/perspective-taking task without emotion regulation (E7). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the NeuroStore extraction for screening.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation (positive and minimizing reappraisal) during stimulus presentation (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7); the sample of healthy adults is reported (I8); the paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. positive reappraisal > natural response, minimizing reappraisal > natural response) (I9); and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps with MNI coordinates are reported (cluster-corrected whole-brain inference, peaks listed) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply: this is empirical primary fMRI activation work (not E3), includes whole-brain results (not E4), reports task activations in addition to connectivity (not E5), contains within-group task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only study (not E7).

The study reports an event-related, task-based fMRI Emotion Regulation Task in which participants were instructed to reappraise or distract vs view sad visual images (visual stimuli: sad and neutral images). Within-task contrasts relevant to emotion regulation are reported (Sad Reappraise > Sad View; Sad Distract > Sad View) as within-group contrasts and as cross-subject regressions with BDI. Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise group-level GLM results with peak coordinates reported in tables. Thus the paper satisfies inclusion criteria I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation including reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), and I11 (acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-only, not non-empirical, and includes within-group task effects).

This task-based fMRI study used visual emotional face stimuli and reports a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (faces > shapes) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise peaks in MNI coordinates. The sample (older adults with MDD and controls) is acceptable. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), which this paper provides. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results reported; within-group effect present).

The paper is a task-based fMRI study with visual socioaffective stimuli and reports whole-brain, corrected, group-level coordinates (I5, I7, I8, I10, I11 satisfied). However, the NeuroStore document shows only a between-group interaction (group × socioaffective condition) linked to task performance; no within-group emotion regulation contrast or an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation is reported. Therefore it meets exclusion E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria I6 (instructed emotion-regulation strategy) and I9 (reports a within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrast) are not met based on this document. Consequently the study is excluded.

This study instructs emotion regulation (down-regulation) during viewing of visual pictures (I5, I6, I7 satisfied) and reports within-task contrasts (view > regulate and regulate > view; I9 satisfied). However, all task-related results are reported using small-volume correction within an amygdala ROI (FWE SVC), and connectivity analyses are ROI/PPI or resting-state seed-based. No group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates in standard space is reported. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E4 (reports only ROI/SVC results with no accompanying whole-brain task analysis) and does not meet inclusion criterion I10. Full text is available within the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This is a task-based fMRI study that explicitly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive social distancing/reappraisal) while participants view visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and photographs). The study reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (engage > view; disengage > view; victim–offender > neutral) and provides whole-brain, voxelwise results with reported MNI peaks. Sample (n=24 healthy adults, females) is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and the task involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking). All inclusion criteria I5–I11 are satisfied.

Excluded because the study does not test regulation of emotional responses to visual stimuli and reports only between-group interaction contrasts with no within-group task effect. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed acceptance/meditation strategy is used, which falls under adjacent antecedent-focused strategies), I8 (sample eligible; patient and control groups reported), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates reported), I11 (results reported in tables/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli are not visual emotional stimuli; stimulus was the word “Meditate”/instructions rather than pictured emotional stimuli), I9 (no clear within-task emotion-regulation contrasts such as reappraise>look; only interaction/between-group contrasts were reported). Because E6 is met, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record shows this is an event-related, task-based fMRI study that instructs participants to increase or decrease their affective responses to visual IAPS images (meets emotion-regulation instruction). It reports within-subject contrasts directly comparing regulation and attend/watch conditions (e.g., increase > attend, decrease), and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in Talairach and cluster-level correction. Sample characteristics (n=29, ages 61–65) are acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI using an instructed cognitive control strategy (‘reality checking’) during anticipation; visual emotional stimuli (IAPS images); reports within-task contrasts (expectation negative>neutral, unknown>neutral, positive>neutral) and between-group regulation vs no-regulation interactions; group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with reported peak coordinates (Talairach). No exclusion criteria are met (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group effects, not an empathy/perspective task without regulation instructions). Analyses and reporting (tables of peaks, whole-brain inference threshold) provide usable coordinates for meta-analysis.

All inclusion criteria are met: (I5) study is task-based fMRI (Emotion Regulation Task); (I6) regulation was explicitly instructed (arrow cues to reduce negative or positive emotions); (I7) stimuli are visual (IAPS pictures and images); (I8) sample is eligible (healthy adult participants reported separately); (I9) within-task regulation contrasts are reported (e.g. viewing > regulate and regulate > view contrasts, within-group); (I10) whole-brain group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (second-level random-effects one-sample t-tests with MNI coordinates and tables of peaks); (I11) whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only reporting, no connectivity-only analyses, no between-group-only contrasts, not an empathy-only task). The NeuroStore extraction lists whole-brain contrasts, conjunction and coordinate tables (tbl1/tbl2) and reported peaks, supporting inclusion.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion regulation task (enhance, suppress, attend; cognitive reappraisal training) (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7); the sample is a clinical patient group which is acceptable (I8); the analysis includes a within-task, within-group cross-subject regression relating regulation-related fMRI activity to HAMD trajectory (a regulation-related contrast) (I9); the analysis is whole-brain, voxelwise with reported peak coordinates in MNI space and corrected cluster inference (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and include within-group effects (no E3–E7 violations). Reported peaks (Table t1) and whole-brain correction further support eligibility. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED in the review.

Exclusion E6 applies: the reported fMRI results are presented only as between-group interactions (Group × Time contrasts) with no within-group task effects reported for any group. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: pictures of foods/vegetables/water), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (contains unregulated viewing contrasts such as high-fat/high-sugar > vegetables or water), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates), I11 (peaks reported in a table). Inclusion not met: I6 (no emotion-regulation instruction during the scanned tasks — instructions explicitly state “do not apply cognitive reappraisals during exposure,” and the reward task had no regulation instructions). Because the study reports only between-group/interactions without any within-group task activation maps, it meets exclusion E6 and therefore must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (cognitive reappraisal: Reappraise vs Maintain) using visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). Participants: healthy sample (n=49) with demographic screening. The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to regulation (Reappraise>Maintain and Maintain>Reappraise). Analyses include group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI (tables reported) and whole-brain corrected inference. Although connectomic PPI connectivity is reported, the study also reports whole-brain task activation contrasts, so it does not meet exclusion E5. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10,I11 and is includable.

The study is a task-based fMRI study with visual stimuli (food images) and a healthy adult female sample; it reports within-task contrasts (high- vs low-caloric) and a voxelwise FWE-corrected cross-subject regression. However, the meta-analysis requires that the fMRI task include an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g., reappraisal) or clearly unregulated viewing contrasts per the review’s inclusion framework. In this study participants were instructed to view images and experienced an externally applied gustatory manipulation (bitter aftertaste) rather than being instructed to use any cognitive emotion-regulation strategy. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered by the provided document.

This fMRI study directly addresses instructed emotion regulation using cognitive reappraisal of visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). It reports task-based BOLD data (I5), an instructed reappraisal strategy (I6), and visual stimuli (I7). The sample includes two groups (high and low psychosis proneness) reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (Reappraise > Negative; Negative > Reappraise) (I9). Importantly, at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis is reported with peak coordinates and FDR whole-brain correction (Reappraise > Negative; reported peaks/table) satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical fMRI, includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only), and reports within-task effects as well as connectivity. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because study appears to be a perspective-taking/imagery task (participants instructed to vividly imagine themselves performing the depicted activities) with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotional responses; this meets exclusion criterion E7. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—photographs), I8 (eligible sample reported), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts such as exercise>landscape), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal). Although whole-brain task contrasts are reported, the instruction to imagine performing the actions constitutes perspective-taking without regulation and therefore the study does not meet the review’s required experimental paradigm. Full text appears complete for extraction.

Although the study is a task-based fMRI investigation of visual emotional stimuli in healthy participants using an instructed emotion task (SEAT) and reports whole-brain results, the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group contrasts/interactions (DHEA vs placebo), correlations, and PPI connectivity analyses. I find no within-task, within-group task-effect contrasts related to regulation or unregulated viewing (e.g., reappraise>look, down-regulate>maintain, or emotion>baseline) reported for any group. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation task—SEAT described as an emotion regulation/appraisal task), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (whole-brain analyses reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I9 (no within-task contrast of regulation or unregulated viewing reported). Based on these, the study should be excluded.

The study is an fMRI task (Go/No-Go) with visual emotional stimuli and reports whole-brain group results (Table t3) — satisfying I5, I7, I8, I10, and I11. However, participants were instructed to "ignore the distractors" (not to use a specific emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance), so criterion I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy) is not met. Additionally, the reported analyses are cross-subject regressions against ARBS scores and ROI correlations; the document does not explicitly report a within-task contrast corresponding to emotion regulation or an unregulated viewing contrast (e.g., ‘negative > neutral’ or ‘watch negative > neutral’), so I9 is not clearly satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met. Therefore the paper does not meet all inclusion criteria required by the review and is excluded.

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (cognitive reappraisal; I6) during presentation of visual stimuli (IAPS images; I7). The sample (patients with panic disorder) is acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (Reappraisal > Maintain) and unregulated viewing (images > baseline) (I9). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with reported peak coordinates in MNI space and corrected inference (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met: results are whole-brain (not ROI-only), include within-group task effects (not only between-group or connectivity-only), and are empirical. Although sample size is small, the extracted record provides the required whole-brain, within-task coordinates and contrasts for inclusion.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of affective anticipation using visual stimuli in a clinical sample (combat veterans) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (peaks in MNI space). However, it does not report an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (no evidence of reappraisal/acceptance or other regulation instructions) nor does the NeuroStore record identify any within-task contrasts of the form 'regulate > view' or unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., negative > neutral). The reported analysis is a multivariate canonical-correlation linking multimodal imaging measures and symptoms, not a standard within-task emotion regulation or simple emotion > baseline contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I6 and I9 despite meeting other inclusion items.

The study reports only seed-based functional connectivity during anticipation of a public speech (seed-based connectivity, GLM of seed time-series), with no reported whole-brain task-evoked activation map related to emotion regulation. Stimuli were verbal instructions (auditory anticipation), not visual, and participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (no reappraisal/instruction to regulate). Therefore it fails the review’s core inclusion criteria and meets exclusion criteria for connectivity-only reporting.

Excluded because the study does not meet the required inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy). The task manipulated incentive context to alter emotional reactions but participants were not instructed to use a regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, distance, accept) during stimulus presentation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: static face photos), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task emotion contrasts such as negative>neutral and interaction contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). Exclusion criteria met: E7 (perspective-taking/role-assumption without instruction to amplify or dampen emotional responses). Therefore the paper must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because stimuli are word/sentence-based (non-visual), violating inclusion criterion I7. Met inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports unregulated within-task emotion contrasts such as Grief > Neutral and within-group Grief Block contrasts), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results reported). Did NOT meet: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—task required ignoring semantic content and responding to number of words, not reappraisal or other regulation), I7 (stimuli are grief-related words, i.e., word/sentence stimuli excluded by I7). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 were met. Therefore the study is excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion-regulation strategy (reappraisal/distancing; suppress emotion) during stimulus presentation (I6). Stimuli are visual film excerpts (videos) (I7). Sample is a healthy child group (n=14; ages 8–10) which is eligible (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts of regulation (Reappraisal > No Reappraisal) and emotion (Sadness > No Sadness) (I9). Analyses are reported at the group level with whole-brain spatial scope and peak coordinates in standard space (MNI/Talairach) in tables (I10,I11). Although the inference field notes small-volume correction, the record also indicates whole-brain scope and reports coordinate peaks, satisfying the whole-brain reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria apply.

All inclusion criteria are satisfied: this is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that explicitly instructs cognitive reappraisal (“Reframe”) as the regulation strategy (I6). The emotional stimuli are visual video clips (I7). The sample is a clinical patient group with a waitlist control (I8). The report includes regulation-related contrasts (e.g., reappraise > react; reappraise criticism vs asterisk-counting) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise activation analyses are reported with peak coordinates in Talairach and cluster-corrected inference (I10), and these results are clearly described in the NeuroStore extract (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain activation maps (not only ROIs), includes activation analyses in addition to connectivity, and also contains within-task contrasts (connectivity) — so E4, E5, and E6 do not apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study uses an Emotional Stroop with IAPS pictures (visual stimuli), whole-brain task fMRI, and reports group-level whole-brain coordinate peaks. However, there is no instruction to use an emotion-regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or instructed cognitive control of emotion). The task instructions describe a number-counting task with occasional "view" trials ("make no response on view trials"), not an instructed regulation condition. Therefore Inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met, so the study must be excluded. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (acceptable sample), I9 (within-task unregulated viewing contrasts implied by view trials/condition factor), I10 (whole-brain group-level results with coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria are met.

The NeuroStore record documents a task-based fMRI study (N-back with emotional face distracters) using visual stimuli in a clinical sample, but the reported results are ROI-based between-group interactions (group × condition) with correction confined to an ROI. No within-group or whole-brain group-level, voxelwise task-evoked maps with peak coordinates are reported in the extract, and no instructed emotion-regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal) is described. Therefore the study fails the review’s requirements for whole-brain evidence and for reporting within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts. Exclusion is based on E4 (only ROI results reported) and E6 (results presented as between-group interactions with no within-group task effects reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation), I9 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps reported). Full text appears complete enough in this record to make the determination.

This is a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (Decrease vs Attend) using visual stimuli (images) and an eligible sample, and the abstract describes within-task contrasts (e.g., regulation to stigmatized vs non-stigmatized). However, the NeuroStore record lists only one extracted analysis, a cross-subject ROI-based regression (region-level inference) with no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps or peak coordinates reported in the document. Therefore it fails the requirement for at least one whole-brain, group-level task-evoked statistical map (I10). Because the paper (as represented here) reports ONLY ROI results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Full text is available in this record (not incomplete).

Study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and suppression (I6). Stimuli are visual static images (IAPS/photographs) (I7). Sample is healthy adult participants and reported group-level results (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (NAT, REAP, ESUP; e.g., reappraisal and natural viewing contrasts) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates reported (MNI) and corrected whole-brain inference (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not exclusively between-group contrasts, and the task involves instructed regulation rather than mere perspective-taking. NeuroStore provides whole-brain corrected peaks and detailed contrasts for the instructed regulation conditions, supporting inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive emotion regulation (I6; abstract and task description indicate cognitive regulation/reappraisal). Stimuli are visual static pictures (fear, disgust, neutral) (I7). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation and unregulated viewing (e.g. Regulation>Perception, Perception>Regulation, within-group fear>neutral) (I9). Whole-brain group-level analyses with reported peak coordinates in MNI space are listed (Analyses 3–6 report whole-brain spatial scope and peaks in Table tbl1; coordinate space MNI is specified), satisfying I10 and I11. Although ROI/SVC analyses are reported for the amygdala, whole-brain task activation maps are also provided, so exclusion for ROI-only results (E4) does not apply. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

The study is excluded because it does not meet all required inclusion criteria. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—film clips), I8 (eligible sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with peak coordinates), I11 (coordinates reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; instructions were to view clips and no regulation was instructed) and I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast or unregulated viewing contrast such as emotion>baseline or watch negative>neutral are reported; reported contrasts test stimulation effects and connectivity). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 are triggered. Full text appears complete for extraction purposes.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the key inclusion requirements for the review. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI; event-related Emotional Stroop task), I7 (visual stimuli: facial images with superimposed emotion words), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups reported separately), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates reported), I11 (whole-brain results clearly described/tabled). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instruction to use an emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal; the task is an emotional conflict/stroop task with no evidence of instructed regulation), I9 (no within-task contrast explicitly reflecting instructed regulation [e.g., reappraise>look] nor a clear unregulated viewing contrast such as emotion>baseline or watch negative>neutral reported). Exclusion IDs met: none (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, within-group maps are reported). Because at least one required inclusion criterion for the review (I6 and I9) is not satisfied, the study is excluded.

The study does not meet the review's key requirement for instructed emotion regulation (I6) and does not report within-task regulation contrasts (I9). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual stimuli (I7), includes an eligible sample (I8), and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I10,I11). However, participants were instructed only to 'look at the presented image' (no instruction to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate), and reported contrasts compare religious vs non-religious images and group interactions rather than explicit regulation vs viewing contrasts (e.g., reappraise>look). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text is complete for screening.

The study is excluded because the emotional stimuli are autobiographical cue phrases (word-based), not visual images or video; this violates inclusion criterion I7 (stimuli must be VISUAL). The study otherwise meets multiple inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion-regulation strategies including acceptance), I8 (sample reported), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported, e.g., accept > feel, feel > accept), and I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is available in the provided NeuroStore record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Excluded because the regulated stimuli are nociceptive (electrical pain to the hand), not visual stimuli as required by I7. The manipulation (self-controlled vs externally controlled painful stimulation) reflects behavioral/perceived control over pain rather than an instructed emotion regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal or an adjacent antecedent-focused instructed strategy, so I6 is not met. The study does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (eligible healthy sample), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation: self-controlled > externally controlled), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results reported), and I11 (whole-brain results reported in tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Therefore the study is excluded solely because it does not satisfy I7 (visual emotional stimuli) and also does not satisfy I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy of the type targeted by the review).

The study reports task-based fMRI of visual emotional stimuli (Affective Picture Viewing Task) with within-task, unregulated viewing contrasts (valence: positive > negative; arousal: high > low). Results are whole-brain, voxelwise, reported with peak coordinates (Talairach) and corrected cluster-level inference. Sample and measures meet criteria. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given, the review objective accepts studies that view stimuli without regulating; thus the absence of an instructed regulation strategy does not preclude inclusion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and reports within-group task effects).

This is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study of instructed emotion regulation (distancing) using visual IAPS images with healthy participants (n=16). It reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (e.g., Distancing > Looking; interaction contrasts Distancing (neg–neu) > Looking (neg–neu)) and unregulated viewing contrasts (Negative > Neutral). Group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI and corrected inference. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I11) and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study reports task-based fMRI with visual stimuli and within-task contrasts and whole-brain results, but the key inclusion criterion I6 (an emotion-regulation strategy is instructed) is not met: the study examines incidental/implicit derogation without instructing participants to regulate their emotions. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (within-task contrasts related to regulation/unregulated viewing), I10 (group-level whole-brain maps with coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria apply.

The record does not provide clear evidence that participants were instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). The extracted analysis is an omnibus main effect of condition from a Go/No-Go task including fearful faces, but no within-task contrast is reported that clearly indexes instructed regulation (e.g., reappraise>look) or an unregulated viewing contrast explicitly tied to emotional stimuli (I9 not demonstrated). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I10 (group-level whole-brain results with reported peaks in standard space). No exclusion criteria are triggered. Because the crucial requirement of an instructed emotion-regulation manipulation (I6) and a clearly related within-task contrast (I9) are not supported by the NeuroStore extraction, the study is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs an emotion regulation strategy (reappraisal; I6), uses visual stimuli (aversive and neutral pictures; I7), includes an eligible sample (healthy adults; I8), and reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (Reappraisal > Maintain; I9). Importantly, the report includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in MNI space and corrected cluster thresholds (analyses 3–6; I10), and these results are clearly described in tables (I11). Although some ROI and connectivity analyses are also reported, whole-brain activation maps are present, so no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be included.

This is a task-based fMRI study with an instructed emotion regulation strategy (reality checking) using visual IAPS pictures and reports whole-brain, corrected peak coordinates (satisfies I5, I6, I7, I10, I11). The sample is a patient group (SAD) with separate assignment to basic vs cognitive-control instruction, so the sample criterion is satisfied (I8). However, the NeuroStore record only reports between-group interaction contrasts (basic group > cognitive-control group) for anticipation and perception; no within-group task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > view or down-regulate > maintain) or unregulated viewing contrasts are reported. Because the paper appears to report only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect, it meets exclusion criterion E6. Therefore the study must be excluded: it fails inclusion criterion I9 and violates E6.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS pictures; I7). The task includes instructed cognitive evaluation (‘Label Pictures’ vs ‘Match Pictures’), which functions as an instructed cognitive strategy/affect-labeling likely serving emotion regulation (I6). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation/unregulated viewing (label > control, match > control, label vs match; I9). Spatial scope is whole-brain with peak coordinates in Talairach and voxelwise corrected results (analyses 4 and 5 report voxel-level corrected associations and peaks), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I10) and coordinate reporting standards (I11). Sample (n=11) is acceptable (I8). Although several contrasts used small-volume correction (ROIs), whole-brain voxelwise results are present, so E4 is not triggered. No exclusion criteria met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is included in the review.

All inclusion criteria are met: task-based fMRI with instructed cognitive reappraisal (decrease trials) using visual IAPS images; within-subject contrasts reported for regulation (decrease negative > look negative) and unregulated viewing (look negative > look neutral); group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates in MNI. No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical, reports whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), includes within-task contrasts (not only between-group or connectivity-only), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking study without regulation instructions. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts (patients vs controls) with no within-group task effects reported, meeting exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI study), I8 (sample eligible; patient and control groups reported), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard space), and I11 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (the task instructs provocation-focused rumination, not an instructed emotion regulation strategy such as cognitive reappraisal or other accepted regulation instructions), I7 (the emotional stimuli are written essays/feedback and rumination statements — word/sentence stimuli rather than visual images or film), and I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated viewing is reported for any group; reported contrasts are between-group interactions). Full text is complete in this NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study is a resting-state effective connectivity (multivariate Granger causality) analysis comparing Depression after Stroke (DAS) and non-depressed stroke (NDAS) patients. It does not involve a task-based fMRI paradigm, has no instructed emotion-regulation task, and uses no visual emotional stimuli. Analyses are connectivity-focused (Granger causality) with no reported whole-brain task-evoked activation maps or within-task regulation contrasts. Therefore it fails the review inclusion criteria requiring task-based emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts and whole-brain task activation results, and meets the exclusion criterion for studies that report only connectivity/resting-state analyses without task activation (E5). Sample reporting is adequate and satisfies I8.

Exclusion criteria met: E5 and E6. This paper reports only seed-based task-modulated connectivity (PPI) results and a between-group interaction contrast (s non-carriers iI > s carriers cI) with no within-group task activation contrasts reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli: facial expressions), I8 (acceptable sample: older adults including clinical subset). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task regulation contrast or within-group task effect reported), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported; only PPI connectivity). Therefore the study must be excluded because it reports only connectivity and between-group interaction results without the required within-task whole-brain activation maps.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation that instructs participants to up- and down-regulate negative emotion (reappraisal), using visual IAPS images, with event-related design and group-level SPM{t} maps reported in ICBM152 space. It reports within-task regulation contrasts (increase>look, decrease>look, increase>decrease, etc.) and provides whole-brain voxelwise results (tables of peak coordinates) alongside some small-volume-corrected findings. Thus all inclusion criteria for the review are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results are reported, not only ROI/SVC or connectivity-only analyses).

The study matches the review objective because participants viewed visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) without instruction to regulate, and the paper reports unregulated viewing contrasts. Specifically: task-based fMRI (I5) with visual IAPS stimuli (I7); healthy sample reported (I8); within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (HA>LA and valence contrasts) are present (I9); multiple analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with reported peak coordinates (Analyses 0–4) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10). Results are reported in tables of peaks (I11). The study does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), but the meta-analysis objective accepts studies that view stimuli without regulating; therefore inclusion is appropriate. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

The study is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional face stimuli and reports whole-brain, group-level activation peaks (satisfies I5, I7, I8, I10, I11). However, the task (Emotional Go/No-Go) instructs response inhibition to certain emotional categories rather than an explicit emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing instructions), so I6 is not met. The reported contrasts are inhibition-related (No-Go > Go) and a between-group interaction; no within-task contrast directly addressing instructed emotion regulation or a simple unregulated viewing contrast (e.g., emotion > baseline) is reported, so I9 is not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria and is excluded.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (standardized aversive pictures) (I7); the sample is a healthy adult group with n=20 reported (I8). It reports within-task contrasts of interest (AV > NE; unregulated viewing contrast) (I9). Importantly, several group-level, whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported with corrected cluster thresholds and peak tables (analyses 4–9), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I10) and acceptable reporting formats (I11). Although NeuroStore labels the task as an "Emotion Regulation Task," the extracted instructions indicate subjects were instructed to look at pictures (i.e., unregulated viewing); the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report ONLY ROI results (whole-brain results are present), is empirical with original fMRI data, and reports within-group task effects. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it meets exclusion criterion E7 (perspective-taking/empathy instruction without explicit emotion regulation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI: mood induction and Go/No-Go tasks), I8 (eligible sample including patient and control groups), I9 (reports within-task emotion contrasts such as anger > neutral), I10 (whole-brain peaks reported in MNI), and I11 (results reported as coordinates/peaks). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—participants were told to take the protagonist’s perspective, not to reappraise or otherwise regulate their emotional response) and I7 (stimuli are auditory/script-driven stories, not VISUAL stimuli). Because the meta-analysis requires instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli, and this study uses auditory perspective-taking mood induction without regulation instructions, it does not satisfy the review’s eligibility and is therefore excluded.

This task-based fMRI study instructed emotion regulation strategies (Suppress and Observe/mindfulness) in response to visual emotional IAPS pictures and includes healthy adult participants (n=21). It reports within-task regulation contrasts (Suppress > Look negative; Observe > Look negative) and an unregulated viewing contrast (Look-negative > Look-neutral). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise with peak coordinates in MNI (reported tables). The study therefore meets all inclusion criteria and does not violate any exclusion criteria (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only).

The study is excluded because it does not meet the review's requirement that the regulated stimuli be emotional visual material (I7). NeuroStore extraction lists only neutral IAPS pictures as stimuli; thus the paradigm does not appear to involve regulation of an emotional response to visual stimuli, which is central to the meta-analysis objective. The study does meet several other inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), includes an instructed emotion-introspection condition that authors interpret as a regulation/acceptance-like strategy (I6), reports within-task contrasts (feel > think; I9), provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I10) and acceptable coordinate reporting (I11), and the participant sample (patients) is an eligible sample (I8). No exclusion criteria from the list are triggered. Because the key requirement about emotional visual stimuli (I7) is not satisfied, the study is excluded.

Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only region-of-interest results reported; inference and correction are within ROI) and E6 (the reported analyses are between-group interactions with no within-group task effects provided). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy: voluntary attentional control to ignore emotional distractors), I7 (visual stimuli: static face images), I8 (sample includes patients and controls reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task or unregulated viewing contrasts reported in the extracted analyses) and I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results; only ROI analyses). Based on the NeuroStore record, the study must be excluded because it reports only ROI-based, between-group interaction results and lacks the required within-group or whole-brain activation contrasts for inclusion in the review.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive reappraisal emotion regulation (I6) using visual IAPS images as stimuli (I7). The sample includes PTSD patients (and a non-PTSD veteran group reported in the document) so the sample criterion is met (I8). The paper reports within-task emotion-regulation contrasts (Reappraise > Maintain) and related within-group and regression analyses (I9). Multiple analyses are described as whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps with peak coordinates in MNI space and cluster-level FWE correction (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not ROI-only or connectivity-only, within-group task effects are reported, and the paper is empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study is a task-based fMRI experiment with visual emotional stimuli and instructed attend/ignore instructions, so it meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed cognitive control/attention to emotional stimuli), I7 (visual stimuli—faces/houses), and I8 (clinical sample with separate controls). However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI)–based (spatial scope: region of interest) with AlphaSim correction within ROIs and no whole-brain voxelwise results, violating I10 and triggering exclusion criterion E4 (ONLY ROI results reported). In addition, the extracted analyses are between-group contrasts and interactions (group main effect and group×attention×emotion interaction) with no within-task (within-group) task-effect contrasts reported, violating I9 and triggering exclusion criterion E6 (ONLY between-group contrasts reported). Because the study fails to provide whole-brain task-evoked maps and reports only between-group/ROI results, it must be excluded.

All required inclusion criteria are met: This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion regulation task (cognitive reappraisal/ distancing instructions; I6) with visual stimuli (IAPS images; I7). The sample (n=73) is acceptable (I8). The report includes a within-task regulation-related contrast (Positive Experience > Positive-Regulate; I9). At least one analysis is a group-level whole-brain voxelwise map with cluster-corrected inference and reported MNI peaks (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the study is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain results (not E4/E5), includes within-group task contrasts (not E6), and the perspective-taking instructions are used as a regulation strategy rather than solely empathy/perspective-taking without emotion regulation (not E7).

This study should be excluded. It is a task-based fMRI study using visual IAPS stimuli with a healthy sample (meets I5, I7, I8). However, it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met) and does not report any within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing whole-brain contrasts (I9 and I10 not met). NeuroStore shows only region-of-interest analyses with small-volume correction (ROI/SVC) and reports between-group interaction contrasts (amber>blue for uncertain>certain), with no whole-brain voxelwise results or within-group task effects presented. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E4 (ONLY ROI/SVC results, no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effects). Because these exclusion criteria are met, the study must be excluded.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation strategies including cognitive reappraisal and suppression (I6). Stimuli are visual videos (sad and disgusting clips) qualifying as visual emotional stimuli (I7). Sample is 20 healthy participants with demographics reported (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise/suppress > watch) (I9). Analyses are group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps with reported peak coordinates in Talairach space (I10) and results are presented in tables (I11). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), within-group contrasts are provided, and the task explicitly instructs regulation (not mere perspective-taking). Therefore the study should be included.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) with an instructed emotion regulation task (participants instructed to naturally experience or actively down-regulate negative emotion) (I6). Stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Sample is healthy participants reported separately (n=55) (I8). Analyses include within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Stim_RegAv > Stim_Av and Stim_Av > Stim_RegAv) (I9). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space and FWE-corrected voxel-level inference (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical issues).

The study reports a task-based fMRI face-processing paradigm with visual stimuli and patient sample, and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (faces > shapes) but all task-evoked activation results are reported as region-of-interest (bilateral amygdala) analyses rather than group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task maps. Therefore it fails the whole-brain evidence requirement (I10) and violates exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results). Also the task did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). Exclusion IDs met: E4. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast faces > shapes). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked maps reported). Full text is complete for screening purposes.

This study meets the review objectives and required criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (faces task) with visual emotional stimuli (NimStim faces). It reports an unregulated viewing contrast (sad > neutral), satisfying the within-task contrast requirement for unregulated viewing. A group-level whole-brain analysis is reported with peak coordinates in standard (Talairach) space and corrected inference (Monte Carlo), so whole-brain evidence is present. The sample (preschool-onset MDD and controls) is acceptable and results for groups are reported. It does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not applicable), but the meta-analysis accepts passive viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: the study includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only) and reports within-task effects. Therefore include.

Excluded because the study does not meet the review's stimulus requirement (I7) and appears to report only between-group contrasts with no within-task regulation contrast (E6). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI; rtfMRI neurofeedback block design), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation-like task: increase neurofeedback via recalling positive autobiographical memories), I8 (clinical sample; PTSD patients acceptable), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise, cluster-corrected results reported), I11 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are not externally presented visual stimuli; regulation targets internally generated autobiographical memories and the only visual stimulus is a feedback bar), I9 (no within-task contrast related to emotion regulation is reported in the document; only a between-group EG>CG contrast is listed). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports only between-group contrast/interactions with no within-group task effect for any group). Full text is complete as provided in this record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

Excluded because the study does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met). The task involves learning cue–emotion pairings and responding to cues/faces, but no instruction to reappraise, distance, accept, or otherwise regulate affect is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task contrast fear>neutral), I10 (whole-brain group-level results with MNI peaks). Exclusion criteria met: none. Therefore excluded for failing required inclusion criterion I6.

The study is a task-based fMRI RCT using instructed cognitive reappraisal (emotion regulation task) with visual IAPS images as stimuli. It reports a within-task contrast directly related to regulation (Reappraisal > Maintain) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (MNI) and corrected inference. All required inclusion criteria (I5–I11) are met. No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain activation maps are reported (not only ROI or connectivity), and within-task effects are present. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the supplied NeuroStore record.

Excluded because the report provides only between-group interaction contrasts with no clear within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts. Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI; Emotional Stroop task, BOLD), I8 (sample acceptable; older adults including clinical and control groups), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise FWE-corrected results with coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal or other explicit regulation instruction; task is an emotional Stroop demanding affective control but not an instructed regulation), I7 (stimuli are emotion words; the protocol excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence stimuli), I9 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts like reappraise>look or emotion>neutral reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (small-volume corrected) task results and uses non-visual verbal 'worry statements' as stimuli, so it does not meet the review’s stimulus and whole-brain reporting requirements. Exclusion criterion met: E4 (ROI/SVC-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: acceptance/suppression/worry), I8 (sample acceptable: clinical GAD group), I9 (within-task regulation contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (stimuli are verbally-presented worry statements, not visual images/films), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level maps reported; analyses are ROI/SVC-only). Because failing any inclusion criterion and meeting E4, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it reports only seed-based task-related connectivity (PPI) results without reporting any whole-brain univariate task-activation map. Exclusion criterion met: E5. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instruction to use cognitive reappraisal/regulation), I7 (visual stimuli - IAPS images), I8 (sample includes adolescents/clinical and control groups acceptable), I9 (reports a task contrast negative > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise PPI map with MNI peak reported), I11 (peaks reported in standard space). Inclusion criteria NOT met: none ([]). Because the only reported whole-brain results are seed-based connectivity (PPI) and no accompanying whole-brain task activation map is provided in the NeuroStore record, E5 applies and the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it reports only seed-based connectivity (gPPI) analyses related to emotional interference and does not report any whole-brain task-evoked activation maps with peak coordinates (Exclusion E5). Although the task is an fMRI task (I5), the sample qualifies (non-patient groups; I8), and there is a within-task emotional contrast (unpleasant vs neutral; I9), the study does not meet the requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation task (I6 not met) and uses word stimuli during a Stroop task (visual words), which the review’s stimulus criterion excludes (I7 not met). Additionally, no whole-brain task activation results are reported (I10 not met). Therefore the paper cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria and meets an exclusion criterion. Exclusion(s) met: E6 (the reported neuroimaging results are presented as between-group genotype contrasts/interactions with no within-group task activation maps reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports an emotion vs neutral contrast: negative > neutral), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise results with MNI peaks). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; participants only pressed a switch to indicate word comprehension—no reappraisal or other regulation instruction), I7 (stimuli are words; the review excludes studies using word/sentence stimuli). Because the study uses word stimuli and lacks any instructed regulation, and because only between-group interaction contrasts are reported without within-group task effects, it is not eligible for this meta-analysis.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (I5) in which participants used cognitive reappraisal to regulate responses to visual appetitive food images (I6,I7). The sample (n=27, age reported) meets the participant criterion (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (Regulate > Look) and choice vs no-choice contrasts (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with cluster-corrected peaks reported in MNI space (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: this is empirical fMRI task activation data with whole-brain results (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical), and it is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion E6 applies: the NeuroStore record shows reported whole-brain results are between-group contrasts/interactions (Analysis_0 labeled as between-group, Analysis_1 an interaction) and the only within-task connectivity is ROI PPI; no within-group task activation (e.g., emotion > baseline or reappraise > look) is reported for any group. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli - faces), I8 (eligible sample and groups reported), I10 (group-level whole-brain map with peak coordinates in MNI reported), I11 (coordinates/tables described). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; task is an emotion matching task with no regulation instruction), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or simple unregulated within-group emotion>control contrast reported — available contrasts are between-group or interactions only). The ROI PPI connectivity analysis does not satisfy I9 because E5 is not triggered (whole-brain maps exist) but E6 excludes this study because of lack of within-group task effects. Full text appears complete in this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is task-based fMRI with visual socio-emotional stimuli (faces, videos) and reports whole-brain coordinate peaks (Talairach) — satisfying I5, I7, I8, I10, I11. However, participants were instructed to 'react normally' or 'just watch' (no instruction to regulate), so I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy) is not met. All reported analyses are between-group interaction contrasts (SAD React > HC Asterisks, etc.) with no within-group regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported for any group, so I9 (within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrast) is not satisfied and Exclusion E6 (ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions reported) applies. Therefore the paper must be excluded from this regulation-focused meta-analysis.

The NeuroStore record shows this is a task-based fMRI study using an instructed emotion regulation task (increase, decrease, attend) with visual IAPS stimuli, conducted in older adults (n=17). It reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g. decrease < attend in the amygdala and VMPFC), and at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates in Talairach and cluster-level correction. These elements satisfy all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply (results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and the task is regulation rather than perspective-taking).

The study is excluded because it does not meet the emotion-regulation task and stimulus-type requirements. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports within-task emotion contrast: unpleasant > neutral and pleasant > neutral), I10 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with MNI coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy—task is an emotion-word Stroop with instruction to attend to color, not to reappraise or otherwise regulate emotion), I7 (emotional stimuli are words; criterion requires visual stimuli such as images or videos and explicitly excludes word/sentence stimuli). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered by the reported methods/results. Full text is available in the provided record (fulltext_incomplete=false). Because failure to satisfy I6 and I7 is sufficient for exclusion, the study should be excluded from this meta-analysis.

The study meets the review objective: participants viewed visual emotional face stimuli and were instructed in task conditions including affect (emotion) labeling versus gender labeling and observe-only conditions. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-related task — affect/emotion labeling — which functions as an instructed regulatory strategy relative to control labeling), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample: healthy adult participants reported), I9 (reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and unregulated viewing: Affect Labeling > Gender Labeling; Observe > Crosshair), I10 (group-level whole-brain analyses with reported peaks and corrected inference), and I11 (results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are reported (so not E4/E5), within-group task effects are present (not E6), and this is empirical fMRI data (not E3); E7 (perspective-taking without regulation) does not apply. Therefore INCLUDE. Note: confidence 0.85 reflecting minor ambiguity about whether affect-labeling is categorized as regulation in all frameworks; the study nevertheless provides appropriate instructed emotion-labeling and clear whole-brain contrasts relevant to the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) task activation results (amygdala) and does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked activation map/contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (ONLY ROI results reported with no whole-brain task activation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: fearful > happy). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; task was implicit gender discrimination with no regulation instruction), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map/contrast reported). Therefore the paper does not satisfy all required inclusion criteria and violates exclusion E4, so it must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This task-based fMRI study uses visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates, and includes a clinical and control group. However, the task did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met) and the NeuroStore extraction shows only between-group interaction contrasts (negative vs neutral comparisons across groups) with no within-group or within-task emotion contrasts (e.g. watch negative > neutral or reappraise > maintain). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample with control group reported separately), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise map with coordinates), I11 (coordinates reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (regulated emotion instruction), I9 (within-task emotion/regulation contrast). Full text is sufficiently represented in the document.

Meets all review inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI with explicit emotion regulation instructions (ENHANCE/SUPPRESS/MAINTAIN) using visual stimuli (MAPS photographs). Sample includes clinical (mTBI) and control groups with separately reported group contrasts. The study reports emotion-regulation contrasts (enhance > maintain) used in group-level analyses and a cross-subject regression, with whole-brain, voxelwise results and peak coordinates reported (Tables 4 and 5) in standard MNI space using cluster-level inference. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not empathy-only).

The study must be excluded because it reports only region-of-interest / small-volume-corrected activation results and seed-based connectivity without a reported whole-brain task activation map. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E4. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports a within-task unregulated contrast sad > neutral). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; task is autobiographical sad recall, not regulation), I7 (stimuli are script-driven imagery and auditory music, not visual stimuli), I10 (no reported whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation map with whole-brain correction — reported activation was SVC/ROI). Details: the main activation contrast (sad>neutral) was reported with small-volume correction within an ROI (amygdala SVC), and the other reported results are seed-based gPPI connectivity analyses. Therefore the paper fails I6, I7 and I10 and meets exclusion E4. Full text appears available in the provided document.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed distraction (MEMORIZE vs VIEW) using visual stimuli (IAPS) in BPD patients and controls with whole-brain voxelwise results reported (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I10, I11). However, the NeuroStore record only documents between-group interaction contrasts (group x time x task) and does not report any standalone within-task regulation contrast or unregulated viewing contrast for any group (e.g., a simple MEMORIZE>VIEW or emotion>baseline reported as a within-group effect). Therefore this appears to meet exclusion criterion E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10, I11. Inclusion criterion not met: I9. Full text was available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest/small-volume-corrected task results (ROI SVC), not whole-brain voxelwise maps (exclusion E4). While it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual emotional stimuli (faces) (I7), includes an eligible sample with control group reported separately (I8), and reports within-task contrasts reflecting implicit emotion regulation/conflict adaptation (I9), it does not meet the requirement that an emotion regulation strategy be instructed (I6) and it does not provide whole-brain evidence (I10). Therefore it fails required inclusion criteria and meets exclusion E4.

The study is excluded because it does not meet the requirement that an explicit emotion-regulation strategy be instructed (I6). While it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual emotional stimuli (faces) (I7), includes an eligible sample (adolescents/healthy; I8), reports within-task emotion contrasts (e.g., fear>happy) consistent with unregulated viewing (I9), and provides group-level whole-brain task-evoked results with coordinates (analyses labelled whole-brain; I10, I11), the task is a Go/No-Go response/inhibition paradigm with instructions to respond or withhold responses to expressions and no instruction to regulate emotion (no reappraisal/acceptance/distancing or other instructed regulation). Therefore I6 is not satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are met.

The paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts (repressors vs sensitizers for angry vs neutral faces) with no within-group task activation contrasts related to emotion regulation or simple viewing (e.g., emotion > neutral) for any group. Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (acceptable sample), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates in MNI), and I11 (results reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; task was social judgment/memorize/rate threat, not reappraisal or other instructed regulation) and I9 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported—only between-group interactions). Full text appears complete in the record. Therefore EXCLUDED under E6.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI) and I8 (sample qualifies: healthy participants reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal; the manipulation is behavioral controllability, not an instructed cognitive regulation strategy), I7 (regulated/evocative stimuli are auditory tones and loud white-noise UCS, not visual emotional stimuli), I9 (no clear within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast relevant to regulation is reported; reported contrasts are between conditions/groups), I10 (results are reported for region-of-interest analyses only; no whole-brain voxelwise results reported). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (ONLY region-of-interest results reported, no whole-brain analysis). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study reports resting-state, seed-based (bilateral amygdala) functional connectivity analyses during a Rest task (participants relaxed and looked at a fixation cross).
