It does not involve a task-based emotion-regulation paradigm or visual emotional stimuli, and it does not report any within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts or task-evoked whole-brain activation maps. Thus it meets exclusion criteria E5 (ONLY seed-based/resting-state connectivity with no whole-brain task activation map) and E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes patients and controls reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation strategy), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map).

The study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) in an event-related attention task (I5, I7). The paradigm explicitly instructed participants to attend or ignore emotional distractors (attentional deployment = instructed cognitive control of emotional response), satisfying the regulation-instruction requirement (I6). Relevant within-task contrasts are reported (attending > ignoring; negative > positive), fulfilling I9. Results are whole-brain, cluster-level corrected, with peak coordinates in MNI space (I10, I11). The sample (ADHD and TD adolescents) is acceptable (I8). No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), not resting-state or only connectivity, and within-task effects are present, so E4, E5, E6 do not apply. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) results with no whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map (Exclusion E4). The paper is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual stimuli (I7) and includes a clinical sample with controls (I8). It reports within-task contrasts (self-referential > general) so a within-task effect is present (I9). However, it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met) and crucially fails the whole-brain requirement (I10 not met) because all reported analyses are ROI-based and inference is corrected within ROI. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment with visual violent vs non-violent video-game stimuli (PLAC Violence > PLAC Non-Violence within-group contrasts present) in a healthy sample (n=38). However, all reported analyses are seed-based whole-brain connectivity results (bilateral amygdala seed) rather than task-evoked activation maps. Exclusion E5 applies: the paper reports ONLY seed-based connectivity analyses without a whole-brain task activation map. Additionally, the task does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). While I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample), and I9 (within-task unregulated viewing contrast) are satisfied, I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map) is not. Therefore the study does not meet the review’s requirement for task-evoked activation data and must be excluded.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: the fMRI task did not instruct an explicit emotion regulation strategy (e.g., reappraise, acceptance, instructed cognitive control). Instead, the task instructed attention to scene or face and threat detection (implicit processing/adaptation). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (sample allowed: adolescents), I9 (reports within-task contrasts including unregulated viewing contrasts such as threatening > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I11 (whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3-E7) apply.

This task-based fMRI study (I5) reports a whole-brain, group-level within-task contrast (math cue > word cue) and provides peak coordinates (I10, I11). Stimuli are visual (arithmetic problems, letter strings) (I7), and the sample is acceptable (I8). The contrast is a within-task comparison that relates to math anxiety (I9). However, the study did not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal or other instructed regulation during anticipation or stimulus), so it fails inclusion criterion I6, which requires an instructed emotion regulation strategy when that is central to the study. No exclusion criteria are met. Because not all mandatory inclusion criteria are satisfied (I6 missing), the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study in which participants were explicitly instructed to regulate their desire for visually presented food images (downregulate by thinking about long-term consequences vs admit/allow desire). The manuscript reports within-task regulation contrasts (REGULATE_TASTY vs ADMIT_TASTY) and unregulated viewing contrasts, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported in MNI coordinates (tables of peaks). Participants are healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not empathy/perspective-taking). Therefore all inclusion criteria for the review are met.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) with adolescent participants including a control group; it reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral, positive > neutral) for groups and individual groups; and it provides whole-brain, voxelwise/group-level results with reported peak coordinates/tables. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), which are present. No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain analyses are reported (so E4 not met), within-group task effects are present (so E6 not met), and this is empirical task activation data (E3 and E5 not met). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Excluded because the study reports only between-group interaction contrasts and does not meet key inclusion criteria for the review. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E6 - only between-group contrasts/interactions are reported with no within-group task effects shown. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups reported separately), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise results with coordinates). (c) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal or similar is described; task is a Go/No-Go), I7 (stimuli are word stimuli, and the review excludes studies using word/sentence stimuli), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported for a group; reported contrasts are between-group interactions). Therefore the study should be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (faces and IAPS pictures; I7). It reports within-group unregulated viewing contrasts (fearful > neutral) for both healthy controls and patients (I9), and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI) (I10, I11). Separate results for patient and control groups are provided (I8). Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts per I9, so the study qualifies. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. Exclusion criteria met: E4, E5, E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: emotional faces), I8 (sample qualifies: clinical and healthy older adults). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; task is face-matching, not an emotion-regulation instruction), I9 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported; only omnibus between-group connectivity contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation map reported; analyses are ROI-based seed gPPI connectivity). The reported analyses are seed-based gPPI ROI connectivity (prefrontal mask) with group-by-worry between-group contrasts; no whole-brain activation coordinates or within-group task effects are provided, so the paper must be excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review’s requirements for emotion regulation of VISUAL stimuli and appears to report only between-group contrasts/interactions without within-task regulation contrasts. Specifically: (a) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI; N-back task), I8 (sample acceptable; patients and controls reported), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with MNI coordinates), I11 (results reported in tables/coordinates). (b) Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy—study used olfactory emotion induction, not reappraisal or other instructed regulation), I7 (stimuli are olfactory: fermented yeast/ambient air, not visual), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported). (c) Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the reported analyses are between-group contrasts and interactions with no within-group task effect for any group). Full text appears complete for screening.

This study is excluded because it appears to report only between-group contrasts/interactions and does not report any within-task (within-group) regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts required for inclusion. Exclusion criterion E6 applies. The document shows whole-brain, task-based fMRI (I5), includes instructed regulation contrasts (I6), uses visual stimuli (I7), reports separate patient and control groups (I8), and provides whole-brain coordinate tables (I10, I11). However it does not report within-group contrasts such as reappraise>look or emotion>baseline (I9 not met); all extracted analyses are group-by-condition interactions or between-group contrasts. Therefore it fails I9 and meets E6.

Excluded because the paper reports only between-group interaction contrasts and no within-group task activation or regulation contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures), I8 (sample includes patients and healthy controls reported separately), I10 (reports whole-brain searchlight analysis corrected across the whole brain with peak coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no clear instruction to perform an emotion regulation strategy; cues indicate expectation but no stated regulation instruction), I9 (no within-task contrast related to regulation or unregulated viewing reported; all reported contrasts are between-group interactions). Because E6 is met, the study must be excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI with visual IAPS stimuli and reports whole-brain within-task contrast (unpleasant > pleasant) correlated with self-compassion; however the task did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (instructions were to rate picture valence), so it fails inclusion criterion I6 which requires an instructed emotion-regulation task. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrast), I10 (whole-brain group-level results with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 are met. Therefore exclude.

The study reports a task-based fMRI emotion regulation experiment using instructed cognitive reappraisal (suppress/re-appraise) with visual IAPS stimuli, includes within-group regulation/viewing contrasts (Maintain>Observe for both groups; Suppress>Maintain contrasts reported), and provides whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (FDR-corrected whole-brain maps reported). Thus it satisfies I5–I11. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and within-group task effects are reported, so E3–E7 are not met.

Excluded under E5: the paper reports only seed-based connectivity (PPI) analyses and does not present any group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation procedure: rtfMRI neurofeedback to upregulate amygdala during happy-memory induction), I8 (sample acceptable: MDD patients), I9 (within-task contrast Happy > Count reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are autobiographical memories with a neurofeedback bar rather than standard visual emotional stimuli such as images/clips), I10 (no task-evoked whole-brain activation map reported — only PPI connectivity maps). Because E5 is met, the study must be excluded.

The study does not meet key inclusion criteria for this review. Although it is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional stimuli (films) and reports whole-brain results (I5, I7, I10) and includes appropriate samples (I8) and report format (I11), the task does not appear to instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). Furthermore, the reported analyses do not include a clear within-task contrast of unregulated viewing (e.g. emotion > neutral or baseline) or an explicit regulation contrast (e.g. reappraise > watch); instead results are correlations with relapse status and a between-group interaction (I9 not met). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 are directly triggered. Therefore the paper must be excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 and I9.

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: there is no instructed emotion-regulation strategy. Participants were instructed to 'pay attention' / 'relax and look' and not to regulate emotional responses. The study does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample includes patient and control groups), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrast: fearful > neutral), I10 (reports whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (results reported in tables/peaks). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Hence excluded for failing I6.

Excluded because the reported analyses are region-of-interest only and present a between-group interaction without reported within-group task effects. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (results corrected within ROI; no whole-brain analysis reported) and E6 (reported contrast is a between-group interaction CET>TAU for emotional vs neutral/no-face conditions with no within-group task effect shown). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed cognitive-control emotion regulation instruction: inhibit responses to emotional distractors), I7 (visual stimuli: faces), I8 (sample acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast reported for any group — only between-group interaction is reported), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates; spatial scope = ROI). Therefore the study cannot be included in the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study (Cyberball) with visual stimuli (animated/prerecorded Cyberball videos) that reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (Observed Inclusion > Observed Exclusion and vice versa). Group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with peak coordinates in MNI space. Sample (n=23 adolescents) is acceptable. Although no emotion-regulation instruction is reported (I6 not met), the meta-analysis permits unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), so the study meets the review’s requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only results, connectivity-only, non-empirical, between-group-only contrasts, or excluded empathy-only paradigm with perspective-taking instructions) apply based on the provided record.

The study is a task-based fMRI with visual stimuli and reports whole-brain coordinate results and unregulated viewing contrasts (disorder-related > neutral). It therefore satisfies I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (eligible sample with patient and control groups), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast), I10 (whole-brain analysis reported), and I11 (coordinates/tables reported). However, the task did not instruct any emotion regulation strategy—participants performed a feature-based comparison (Emotional Stroop) with task-irrelevant scenes and were not instructed to regulate emotion—so inclusion criterion I6 is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study must be excluded for failing I6.

This study reports a task-based fMRI neurofeedback training where participants were instructed to volitionally regulate anterior insula activity (recall/imagining negative emotional events during regulation) while viewing painful pictures (visual stimuli). It includes within-task contrasts (regulation > baseline) at the group level with whole-brain, voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates. Sample is healthy adults and analyses include task activation maps alongside connectivity. These meet the review’s requirements for task-based emotion regulation with visual stimuli and whole-brain reporting, and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study with visual face stimuli and whole-brain voxelwise peaks (I5, I7, I10) and an eligible sample (I8). However, there is no indication that participants were instructed to regulate their emotional responses (no cognitive reappraisal or other instructed regulation), so I6 is not met. The reported analyses in the document are between-group interaction contrasts (old happy>neutral > young happy>neutral, etc.) and the extraction lists only these interaction results with no within-group task contrasts or unregulated viewing contrasts; therefore I9 is not satisfied. Because the document reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effects, exclusion criterion E6 applies. Based on these points, the study is excluded.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based, whole-brain fMRI study with visual stimuli and an instructed distraction strategy (meets I5, I6, I7, I8, I10). However, all extracted analyses are described as omnibus between-group contrasts/interactions (e.g., group-by-picture type and group-by-picture type-by-strategy), and the shared contrast field is explicitly 'omnibus, between-group'. The record does not report any within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., distraction > evaluation, reappraise > look) or unregulated viewing contrasts for any group. Because only between-group interactions are reported, this meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (erotic images) and an appetitive Pavlovian conditioning task. It reports within-task contrasts of unregulated viewing/conditioning (CS+ > CS−) and a main effect of stimulus, satisfying the requirement for an unregulated viewing contrast. At least one analysis (CS+ > CS−) is reported as a whole-brain group-level voxelwise map with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space. Although no explicit emotion-regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the review objective allows inclusion of studies that include unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), so the study meets the other required criteria. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI or only connectivity results) apply because whole-brain activation maps are reported.

This study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I6: there is no instructed emotion-regulation strategy. Participants underwent a Cyberball social rejection task and trait mindfulness was measured, but participants were not instructed to regulate their emotions (no reappraise/accept/distancing instructions). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—computerized Cyberball), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports a within-task contrast: rejection > acceptance), I10 (group-level whole-brain results reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed regulation). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete for screening.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed emotion regulation (distance vs. immerse cues), using visual IAPS images, in a sample of patients with BPD. It reports within-task regulation contrasts (distance/aversive > immerse/aversive) and unregulated viewing contrasts (immersive aversive > neutral). At least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis is reported (analysis 5: whole-brain, uncorrected cluster threshold with reported peaks) in MNI space; other analyses include ROI/SVC results but these do not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are present. Thus it meets all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study with visual emotional face stimuli and an instruction to attend to letters while ignoring faces (meeting I5, I6, I7, I8), the NeuroStore record shows only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and seed-based PPI connectivity contrasts and reports group-level between-group contrasts/interactions. No within-group task activation contrasts (e.g. emotion > neutral or reappraise > look) or any whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps with peak coordinates are reported. Therefore the study violates exclusion criteria E4 (ROI-only/small-volume-corrected results with no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effects). Inclusion criteria I9 and I10 are not satisfied. Exclude on this basis.

The study uses script-driven mental imagery delivered via audio (no visual stimuli), so it fails inclusion criterion I7 (visual stimuli required). Additionally, the task evokes stress via imagery rather than instructing an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). It does meet several inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I5), includes a within-task contrast (Stress > Neutral; I9), reports whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard space (I10 and I11), and sample criteria are acceptable (I8). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Because the stimuli are non-visual (script-driven auditory imagery) and regulation instructions are not present, the study does not match the meta-analysis focus and is excluded.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is an fMRI task study (I5) using instructed emotion regulation (explicit verbal suppression and implicit priming) (I6), with visual stimuli (IAPS and other images) (I7). The sample is healthy participants (n=17) so eligible (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (e.g., IMP > EXP, BASEEXP > EXP, interactions with memory performance) (I9). Multiple analyses are whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates reported in Talairach space and cluster-corrected inference (I10), and results are presented as tables of coordinates (I11). No exclusion criteria apply: results include whole-brain activation maps (not ROI-only), task activation contrasts (not only connectivity or between-group effects), and the paradigm is regulation of emotional responses rather than perspective-taking. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (positive reappraisal) (I6) applied to visual stimuli (IAPS pictures) (I7). It includes an appropriate within-task regulation contrast (Positive Reappraisal > Negative Attend) (I9) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results in MNI space with peak coordinates (corrected whole-brain inference, reported peaks) (I10, I11). The sample (clinical patients) is acceptable under I8. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical (not E3), reports whole-brain analyses rather than only ROI (not E4), is not limited to connectivity or resting-state (not E5), includes within-group task effects (not E6), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking task without regulation instructions (not E7).

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation (I5) using visual stimuli (photographs) (I7) in an eligible adolescent clinical sample (overweight girls) (I8), and reports whole-brain peak coordinates in standard space (MNI) for task contrasts (I10). However, it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). The extracted analyses are predominantly between-group contrasts and interactions (group × feedback, group × peer value, etc.), and the document does not report any within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., negative > neutral) or within-group regulation contrasts; thus the paper appears to report ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect for any group (exclusion E6 applies). Because I6 and I9 are not satisfied and E6 is met, the study does not meet the review’s inclusion criteria.

The study reports an event-related task-based fMRI emotion regulation experiment using visual stimuli (IAPS images) with instructed regulation strategies (increase/decrease/maintain; reappraisal-like and instructed outcomes). It includes within-task contrasts of interest (enhance > suppress) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (cluster-level GRF-corrected). The sample is an eligible participant group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, not empathy-only). Thus all relevant inclusion criteria for the review are met.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment (working memory task with emotional distracters) using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS scenes and faces). It includes a within-task unregulated viewing contrast (main effect of distracter types; negative vs neutral) and reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results with peaks in MNI space (FWE-corrected). The sample includes OCD patients and healthy controls and results are reported at the group level. Although no explicit instruction to regulate (I6) is described, the meta-analysis accepts unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., watch negative > neutral), so lack of a regulation instruction does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met: the paper does not report only ROI or only connectivity analyses and provides whole-brain task activation maps. Therefore it meets the review’s inclusion criteria for unregulated viewing contrasts and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study with visual face stimuli (I5, I7), includes patient and control groups (I8), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I10,I11). However, the task instructions were gender identification (no instruction to regulate emotion), and the reported task activation results are predominately between-group contrasts and interactions (e.g., group × expression contrasts). The record does not report any within-group unregulated viewing contrast (e.g., emotion > baseline or watch negative > neutral) or any within-task regulation contrast. Only a within-group seed-based connectivity finding is reported for HC. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I9 (no within-task activation/viewing contrast) and I6 (no instructed regulation). It meets exclusion E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Consequently it must be excluded.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria: (I5) it is a task-based fMRI study; (I6) it instructs an emotion regulation strategy (REAPPRAISE vs LOOK); (I7) stimuli are visual (IAPS and pictures of alcohol/food); (I9) it reports within-task regulation contrasts (REAPPRAISE-Negative > LOOK-Negative and LATER > NOW); (I10) it provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (FWE-corrected whole-brain contrasts with reported peak coordinates); (I11) peaks are reported in tables. The sample is a clinical population (AUD) which is acceptable under I8. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only reporting).

All three reported analyses are between-group genotype-by-condition interaction contrasts (A-allele carriers vs C/C homozygotes) rather than within-group task contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation including distancing/reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS/EmoPicS), I8 (healthy participant sample), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates), I11 (results presented as coordinate tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I9 (no within-task contrast for any group such as reappraise>look or watch negative>neutral is reported in the extracted document). This pattern meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effects). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment with visual emotional stimuli and reports whole-brain unregulated viewing contrasts and brain-behavior correlations, but participants were instructed to watch and rate pictures (no instructed emotion regulation strategy). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., Neg>Neu), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps reported), I11 (results clearly reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instruction to regulate emotions — no reappraise/distancing/other regulation instruction). No exclusion criteria from E3–E7 apply. Therefore excluded for failing I6.

This study reports only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses of task-evoked BOLD during an affective picture viewing task; NeuroStore indicates all analyses have spatial scope = region of interest and no whole-brain, voxelwise group maps or coordinate tables are reported. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results with no accompanying whole-brain analysis). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures), I8 (sample: adolescents/patients). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; task required affective rating, not regulation), I9 (no within-task regulation or explicit unregulated viewing contrasts such as emotion > neutral are reported in the extracted analyses), and I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task activation maps with peak coordinates). Because E4 is met, the study must be excluded.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI emotion regulation study with visual IAPS stimuli and explicit reappraisal instructions (meets I5, I6, I7) in a clinical (IGD) and control sample reported separately (meets I8). Whole-brain, voxelwise corrected results are reported (meets I10). However, all extracted contrasts are described as omnibus/between-group (group-by-condition interaction and ICA task-relatedness); no within-task contrasts (e.g. reappraise > look or watch negative > neutral) or within-group task effects are reported in the provided document. Therefore exclusion criterion E6 (ONLY between-group contrasts or interactions with no within-group task effect) is met. Inclusion I9 (reports at least one within-task contrast) is not met. Decision: EXCLUDED due to E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I9.

The study reports a task-based fMRI whole-brain analysis of visual emotional stimuli (faces) in a patient and control sample, but the NeuroStore record includes only a between-group contrast (Group effect: CD > controls) from the Emotion model and does not report any within-group task effects or unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral) for either group. Inclusion met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with coordinates), I11 (results reported in table). Inclusion not met: I9 (no within-task or unregulated viewing contrast reported). Exclusion met: E6 (only between-group contrast reported with no within-group task effect). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports passive viewing of emotional facial photographs with instructions to rate feelings and explicitly states there were no instructions to regulate emotional reactions. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy). It does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: photographs of faces), I8 (eligible sample: healthy participants reported separately), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts such as negative > neutral), I10 (group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with peak coordinates in MNI), and I11 (results reported in tables). No exclusion criteria from the list are met. Because I6 is not satisfied, the paper must be excluded.

This study reports resting-state seed-based functional connectivity analyses (left and right OFC) examining associations with HAM-D/HAM-A in marijuana-using adolescents. It is NOT a task-based fMRI study of emotion regulation or viewing of visual emotional stimuli. It therefore fails required inclusion criteria for task-based emotion-regulation studies and reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity without any task activation contrasts, meeting exclusion criterion E5. Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample of adolescents is acceptable). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task/regulation or viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain task-evoked activation map). Exclusion criteria met: E5 (only seed-based/resting-state connectivity reported, no whole-brain task activation map).

The study meets the review’s requirements for inclusion as a passive viewing/visual-emotion fMRI study. It is a task-based fMRI study using visual film/video stimuli (six videotapes) and reports within-task condition effects (main effect of condition, and condition × genotype interaction) from a whole-brain voxelwise analysis with peak coordinates in Talairach and cluster-level FWE correction. The sample (PG and HC groups) is acceptable. Although no instructed emotion-regulation strategy is reported (I6 not satisfied), the meta-analysis objective and criterion I9 allow unregulated viewing contrasts; the reported main effect of condition provides the necessary within-task (unregulated viewing) contrasts. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group contrasts) apply. Therefore the paper is eligible for inclusion.

The NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (controls decrease-negative > bipolar observe-negative) and seed-based PPI connectivity, with no evidence of any within-task contrasts (e.g., reappraise > attend or down-regulate > maintain) reported for either group. Whole-brain group-level maps with peak coordinates are present, and the task is a visual emotion-regulation task with instructed cognitive reappraisal. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation/cognitive reappraisal), I7 (visual stimuli), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps with coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrast reported). I8 (separate within-group results for controls) is also not supported by the document. Hence excluded.

Excluded because the study does not meet the emotion-regulation task and stimulus-type requirements. No exclusion criteria (E3-E7) are triggered. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., drug > neutral and within-group effects), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with Talairach coordinates), and I11 (results reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instruction to regulate emotion — task is a rewarded cue-reactivity button-press, not reappraisal/distancing/other instructed regulation), and I7 (stimuli are word stimuli; the review excludes studies whose regulated or viewed stimuli are words/sentences). Because I6 and I7 are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and necessary inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual emotional stimuli (film/video clips) (I7), includes eligible samples (children and adults; healthy) (I8), reports an unregulated viewing contrast (Negative > Neutral within children) relevant to the review (I9), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard space (MNI) (I10,I11). Although no regulation instruction was given (I6 not met), the review accepts unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or only between-group effects). Therefore include.

This study does not meet key inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It is a task-based fMRI study with whole-brain, group- and within-group contrasts of anticipatory anxiety to conditioned visual cues (I5, I9, I10, I11) and includes an eligible sample (I8). However, participants were not instructed to use an emotion-regulation strategy (violates I6), and the primary emotional stimulus is thermal (heat) delivered to the forearm rather than a visual emotional stimulus (violates I7). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore, exclude because it fails I6 and I7.

The study is a task-based whole-brain fMRI study of working memory with visual emotional distractors, but it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (no reappraisal/explicit regulation instruction) and reports only between-group interaction contrasts rather than within-group regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (clinical and control groups reported), I10 (whole-brain group-level results with coordinates), I11 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts reported). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Therefore exclude.

Study reports only between-group interaction contrasts (PBD vs HC for angry>neutral and happy>neutral) without reporting any within-group emotion>neutral or simple viewing contrasts, and does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy. This meets exclusion E6 (only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). It does meet task-based fMRI (I5), visual face stimuli (I7), sample criteria (I8), whole-brain voxelwise reporting with standard-space peaks (I10), and acceptable reporting (I11). It does not meet I6 (no instructed regulation) and does not provide within-task unregulated viewing contrasts for any group (I9). Full text is complete in the provided record.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual emotional stimuli (IAPS) and an oddball event-related task. The paper reports within-group contrasts comparing aversive and target conditions (aversive > target; target > aversive) for both healthy controls and schizophrenia patients, with whole-brain voxelwise inference and reported peak coordinates in MNI. Both patient and control groups are reported separately. Although no explicit instruction to regulate emotion (e.g., reappraisal) is described, the meta-analysis objective includes both regulation and unregulated viewing contrasts; this study provides unregulated viewing contrasts that match inclusion criterion I9. Therefore it meets task-based fMRI (I5), visual stimuli (I7), sample reporting (I8), within-task/unregulated viewing contrast (I9), whole-brain voxelwise reporting with coordinates (I10), and acceptability of coordinate reporting (I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete in the record.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. The task is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs cognitive control over automatic emotional actions (an instructed emotion-regulation/control strategy rather than mere viewing) meeting I6. Stimuli are visual (facial expressions) meeting I7. Sample is an eligible human participant group (healthy police recruits) meeting I8. The paper reports within-task contrasts related to emotion regulation (incongruent > congruent) meeting I9. At least one analysis (Analysis 0) is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation map with peak coordinates in MNI and FWE whole-brain inference, satisfying I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper does not report only ROI/SVC results (it includes whole-brain results), nor only connectivity-only analyses, nor only between-group contrasts. Therefore INCLUDE.

This study reports resting-state functional connectivity (rest task, eyes closed) and a between-group amygdala × group interaction from observational cohorts; there is no task, no visual emotional stimuli, and no instructed emotion regulation or within-task regulation/viewing contrasts. Exclusion criteria E5 (resting-state/seed-based connectivity only, with no whole-brain task activation map) applies; E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-task task effect) also applies. Inclusion criterion I8 (sample includes patient and control groups) is met. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task regulation or viewing contrasts), and I10 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and should be excluded.

Exclusion: E4 (ONLY region-of-interest results reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: alcohol pictures), I8 (sample: clinical alcohol-dependent patients), I9 (unregulated viewing contrast reported: alcohol > neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; study is cue-exposure/open-label HF-rTMS, not a regulation task), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group analysis: spatial scope reported as region-of-interest and inference corrected within ROI). The study therefore fails I6 and I10 and meets exclusion E4, so it must be excluded from this meta-analysis.

This task-based fMRI study uses an Approach-Avoidance Task requiring instructed cognitive control over automatic emotional action tendencies (incongruent > congruent), with visual face stimuli and healthy adult participants (n=279). It reports within-task contrasts (incongruent > congruent) that index emotion-action regulation and provides whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space. Although small-volume correction was applied for inference, the NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain spatial scope and reports peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI face-processing study with visual stimuli and both patient and healthy groups. It reports an emotion > control (condition) contrast, but the reported analysis is region-of-interest (spatial scope: region of interest) rather than a group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation map; no whole-brain results are provided in the document. The task instructed a color-detection button press (not an emotion-regulation instruction), so no instructed regulation (I6) is present. Because the study reports only ROI results and lacks whole-brain task activation maps, it violates inclusion criterion I10 and meets exclusion criterion E4. Therefore it must be excluded.

This study used resting-state fMRI (instruction: fixate, do not think) and reports ALFF and seed-based connectivity results rather than any task-evoked emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts. Exclusion E5 applies: only resting-state / connectivity analyses are reported with no whole-brain task activation map. Inclusion met: I8 (sample criteria: older adults, patients and controls reported). Inclusions NOT met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I9 (within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). Therefore the study does not address the review objective and must be excluded.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective as an fMRI task in which participants view emotional visual stimuli (masked happy and fearful faces) without instructed emotion regulation. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli—photographs of faces), I8 (sample includes patient group and control group reported separately), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g. masked angry>neutral and masked happy>neutral, both within-group and between-group), I10 (reports whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates/tables), and I11 (results are reported in tables of coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper reports whole-brain task activation maps (so E4, E5 not met), it includes within-group task effects (so E6 not met), and it is empirical fMRI data (so E3 not met). Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given, the meta-analysis scope explicitly accepts unregulated viewing contrasts. Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

The NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (group x load x emotion) and does not report any within-group or simple within-task emotion viewing contrasts (e.g., emotion > neutral within HC or SZ). Therefore the study provides whole-brain, task-based fMRI data with visual emotional stimuli and a clinical and control sample (I5, I7, I8, I10, I11 met), but it appears to report ONLY between-group/interaction contrasts with no within-group task effect reported, which meets exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy reported) and I9 (no within-task within-group emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast reported in the extracted analyses).

This task-based fMRI study used visual emotional stimuli (validated images) and reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (negative > neutral) at the group level with whole-brain voxelwise inference and peak coordinates in MNI space. The sample (adult women) is eligible. Although participants were instructed to indicate each image as unpleasant or neutral (an evaluation task rather than an instructed emotion-regulation strategy), the review objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts; the reported negative>neutral contrasts satisfy that requirement. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis objective and the required whole-brain reporting standards.

Exclusion(s) met: E6 - the NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts (GAD > controls and controls > GAD for worry induction/suppression); no within-group task activation contrasts are provided. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based MRI/perfusion task), I6 (an instructed emotion-regulation strategy: worry suppression/recall of pleasant memory), I8 (sample with patient and control groups), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI), I11 (results reported as peaks/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I7 (emotional stimuli are NOT visual — they are individualized worry statements and eyes-closed imagery/script-driven recall), I9 (no within-task regulation contrasts such as reappraise>look reported for any group). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis focused on regulation of visual emotional stimuli and on studies reporting within-task regulation contrasts.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment with instructed down-regulation of emotional responses to visual (aversive) pictures and reports within-task contrasts (regulate > view) and peak coordinates, so it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9 and I11. However, all reported analyses in the NeuroStore record are seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity (gPPI and DCM) results and the record contains no whole-brain task-evoked activation map or activation contrast results. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E5 (studies that report ONLY seed-based connectivity/effective connectivity analyses without also reporting a whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criterion I10 (a group-level whole-brain task activation map) is not met. Based on these elements, I exclude the study from the meta-analysis.

The study is a task-based fMRI whole-brain investigation with visual stimuli and reports unregulated viewing contrasts (fearful > neutral) for both groups and provides peak coordinates (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, participants were instructed to watch the movie sequences passively; no emotion regulation strategy (acceptance or other) was instructed during the task. Although habitual acceptance was measured via EAQ and used as a regressor, this reflects individual differences, not an instructed regulation condition. Therefore inclusion criterion I6 (an emotion regulation strategy instructed during the fMRI task) is not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Exclude the study.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual face stimuli in adolescents and reports whole-brain group analyses with peak coordinates, so it meets I5, I7, I8, I10 and I11. However, it does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (task is a gender identification/face-processing task), so I6 is not met. Crucially, the NeuroStore record shows reported results are omnibus between-group effects and group×emotion interactions (between-group contrasts and PPI connectivity differences) with no within-group task contrasts (e.g., emotion > baseline or “look” vs “reappraise”) reported. Therefore it fails I9 and meets exclusion criterion E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Because of E6 and missing required inclusion criteria (I6 and I9), the study must be excluded.

This study reports an event-related, task-based fMRI experiment using visual emotional stimuli (trauma-related vs neutral pictures) with whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses correlating neural activation with subsequent PTSD severity. It therefore meets I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable—patient group), I9 (reports an unregulated viewing contrast: trauma-related > neutral), I10 (whole-brain group-level peak coordinates reported), and I11 (results reported in tables). However, the task involved passive viewing/symptom provocation with instructions to view attentively (no instruction to regulate emotion, reappraise, or otherwise control emotional response). Therefore it does NOT meet I6 (emotion regulation strategy instructed). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are triggered. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied, the study is excluded for failing I6.

This study is excluded because all reported task analyses are region-of-interest (ROI)-restricted and the paper reports only between-group × time interaction contrasts with no within-task (e.g. reappraise > look) or unregulated viewing contrasts for any group. Specifically, exclusion criteria met: E4 (ONLY ROI results reported; no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (ONLY between-group/interactions reported without any within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (instructed emotion regulation: reappraise instructions), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS pictures), I8 (sample allowed: clinical nicotine-dependent group with a control group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I9 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrast reported), I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise maps; analyses corrected within ROI only). Full text appears complete enough for screening. Therefore exclude.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment instructing participants to regulate emotional responses (increase/decrease) to visual IAPS pictures, with relevant within-task contrasts (e.g., decrease > watch) reported. The document lists whole-brain spatial scope, peak coordinates in MNI space, and tables of reported peaks, indicating group-level voxelwise results. Although the inference notes small-volume correction within ROIs, the presence of whole-brain scope and coordinate tables satisfies the requirement for whole-brain evidence. The sample is healthy adults and the contrasts map directly onto the meta-analysis objective of instructed emotion regulation of visual stimuli.

The NeuroStore record shows a task-based fMRI study with instructed emotion regulation (compassion vs reappraisal) using visual IAPS stimuli and whole-brain voxelwise analysis. However, the only reported neuroimaging analysis in this document is a Group × Looking Time omnibus between-group interaction (whole-brain). The record does not report any within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., reappraise > look, regulate > maintain) or unregulated viewing contrasts. Therefore the study appears to report only between-group interaction results and lacks within-group task effects, failing inclusion criterion I9 and meeting exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I9. Exclusion criteria met: E6. Full text appears available in this record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This task-based fMRI study instructs cognitive emotion regulation (reappraisal) during trials (I6). Stimuli are visual (colored squares) (I7). Participants (n=12, healthy adults) are reported (I8). The paper reports within-task regulation contrasts (e.g. Regulate CS+ > Attend CS+, Attend CS+ > Regulate CS+) (I9). Multiple group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses with voxelwise inference and peak coordinates in Talairach are present (e.g. Analyses 5–8 report whole-brain voxelwise results and tables of peaks) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I10). It is a task-based fMRI BOLD study (I5). No exclusion criteria are met: the study includes whole-brain activation maps (so not E4 or E5), reports within-group task contrasts (not E6), and is not a non-empirical or empathy-only perspective-taking paper (not E3 or E7). Therefore all required inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply. Detailed reporting of ROI analyses is present but does not preclude inclusion because whole-brain results are also reported.

This study is a task-based fMRI study using visual face stimuli in patients and healthy controls and reports whole-brain, coordinate-based results (I5, I7, I8, I10, I11 satisfied). However, the task instructions are emotion induction (“Try to become as happy [sad] as possible”), not an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). NeuroStore indicates the reported analyses are omnibus, between-group contrasts (group x time ANOVA) with no within-group task effects or within-task regulation contrasts reported; thus there are no within-task contrasts of regulation or even unregulated viewing for any group (I9 not met). Because the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect, it meets exclusion criterion E6. Therefore exclude.

Excluded because the study does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI: event-related emotional go/no-go), I7 (visual stimuli: KDEF faces), I8 (sample: healthy participants reported separately), I9 (reports within-task emotional contrasts: happy/no-go > sad/no-go and correct no-go > null), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates, FWE-corrected), I11 (results reported in text/tables). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 apply). Reason for exclusion: fails to meet I6 — there was no instruction to regulate emotion (reappraisal, distancing, acceptance, or other instructed cognitive regulation); the task measured attentional disengagement/inhibition but not instructed emotion regulation. Full text was available for screening (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation using visual emotional face stimuli and reports whole-brain, group-level activation maps (analyses include emotions > shapes contrasts, FWE and AlphaSim-corrected results). It therefore meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11. However, the task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy; participants performed a color-identification task making the emotion processing implicit/irrelevant, so I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be satisfied and I6 is not met, the study is excluded.

No explicit instruction to use an emotion regulation strategy was reported. The study used an emotional Stroop paradigm in which participants performed a demanding cognitive (numerosity) task while viewing IAPS pictures; contrasts include unregulated viewing (view > congruent/incongruent), whole-brain task activations and seed-based connectivity. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (contains unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (whole-brain group-level maps with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy such as reappraisal, suppression, or explicit instructed cognitive regulation). No exclusion criteria were triggered (E3–E7 not met). Conclusion: excluded because it does not meet I6 (instruction to regulate emotion), despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

Excluded because the report contains only region-of-interest (ROI) analyses and appears to report only between-group/simple effects rather than within-task whole-brain contrasts. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (ONLY ROI / small-volume-corrected results reported) and E6 (ONLY between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: faces/houses), I8 (sample includes clinical and control groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instruction to regulate emotion reported), I9 (no clear within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast reported — reported contrasts are between-group simple effects), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with peak coordinates reported). Because at least one exclusion criterion is met and several required inclusion criteria (I9/I10/I6) are not satisfied, the study is excluded.

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria for an emotion-regulation meta-analysis. Although it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), includes an acceptable sample (I8), and reports a whole-brain group-level contrast (I10) with coordinate peaks (I11), it does NOT instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6), uses word stimuli (swear/affective words) which are excluded by the stimulus criterion (I7), and does not report any within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast for a group (I9). The reported whole-brain result is a between-group interaction and the only within-group finding is an ROI correlation, so exclusion criterion E6 (only between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect) applies.

Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: face images), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (group-level whole-brain, voxelwise multivariate maps with reported peaks), I11 (results reported as tables/peaks). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy — tasks were impression-formation and ratings, not instructions to reappraise/accept/distancing or otherwise regulate emotional responses), I9 (no within-task contrast examining instructed regulation vs viewing or an unregulated viewing contrast; analyses are cross-subject regressions of EMS and PLS coactivation). The study therefore does not meet the core requirement that an emotion-regulation strategy be instructed and contrasted. Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the review's requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation task (I6) nor does it report any within-task contrast explicitly related to emotion regulation (I9). The task is a mood/emotion induction instructing participants to 'use [faces] to help you feel happy/sad' (perspective-taking/empathic induction), not an instructed regulation strategy such as reappraisal. Applicable exclusion criterion E7 (empathy/perspective-taking studies with no instruction to amplify or dampen one’s emotional response in the sense of regulated modulation) is therefore met. The study does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise maps reported with peak coordinates), and I11 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 and I9.

This is a task-based fMRI study that directly instructs an emotion regulation strategy (attention-to-breath, an instructed mindfulness regulation) and compares regulated vs passive viewing of aversive visual stimuli (IAPS pictures). The paper reports within-task contrasts related to regulation (ATB > PV, PV > ATB, interactions) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates and FWE-corrected maps. Sample is healthy adults (n=26). No exclusion criteria are met (not a review, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups-only, not an empathy/perspective-taking task). Therefore it meets all review inclusion criteria.

This is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructs emotion regulation (enhance/suppress/maintain) qualifying as instructed cognitive reappraisal/regulated control (I6), uses visual IAPS pictures as stimuli (I7), and includes an MDD patient group (n=27) which is an eligible sample (I8). It reports the within-task regulation contrast positive suppress > positive maintain (I9) and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with Talairach coordinates, cluster correction, and reported peaks (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria apply: the paper is empirical, reports whole-brain activation (not ROI-only), includes within-task effects (not only between-group or connectivity), and is not an empathy/perspective-taking-only task. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

Excluded because the paper reports only region-of-interest (ROI) task results with no whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps (Exclusion E4). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: Ekman facial images), I8 (sample: healthy participants), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts: faces > forms, forms > faces). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy; task involved face identity matching without reappraisal or other regulation instructions), I10 (no whole-brain evidence; spatial scope is ROI-only). Full text record appears complete for screening.

The study does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). The task is an identity-matching task with fear vs neutral contrast (unregulated viewing), and although the abstract discusses possible implicit reappraisal, there is no experimental instruction to regulate. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task emotion contrast: fear simple effect), I10 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates), I11 (coordinates reported in tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). No exclusion criteria are met (E3- E7 not applicable). Full text is complete as provided.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment with instructed emotion regulation (thought suppression: Don't Think vs Think), reports within-task regulation contrasts, and provides whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates (I5, I6, I9, I10, I11 met). Sample inclusion is acceptable (I8 met). However, the regulated stimuli are written relationship scenarios (text/written instructions), not visual images or film stimuli; the review’s stimulus criterion excludes studies whose regulated stimuli are word/sentence/script-driven imagery (I7 not met). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Therefore the study must be excluded because it fails inclusion criterion I7.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) that instructed participants to decrease emotional reactions via reinterpretation (cognitive reappraisal) (I6). Stimuli were visual pictures (moral and non-moral) (I7). The sample comprises healthy adult participants reported separately (I8). The report includes within-task regulation contrasts (e.g., Decrease Moral > Watch Moral; Decrease Non-moral etc.) and unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g., Watch Moral > Odd–Even) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with coordinates in MNI and peaks reported in tables (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria are met (not non-empirical, not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group task effects, and includes explicit regulation instructions).

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment that explicitly instructs cognitive emotion regulation (Regulate: cognitively downregulate distress) and includes unregulated viewing (Attend/Neutral). Emotional stimuli are visual film clips (qualifies as visual). Reported group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates are provided (tables of peaks reported). Relevant within-task contrasts related to regulation are present (Regulate > Attend; Attend/Regulate > Neutral), and both within-group and between-group analyses are reported. Sample size is reported (n=32) and the study population is acceptable. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and not an empathy task without regulation instruction). Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11).

Excluded because the reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) only, with region-level inference and no whole-brain (voxelwise) group maps (Exclusion E4). The study is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual anticipation cues (Red X/Blue O) as stimuli (I7), and the sample qualifies (I8). It reports within-task contrasts involving handholding condition (partner vs alone) and pre/post EFT (I9). However, it does NOT meet the requirement that an emotion regulation strategy was instructed (I6)—the manipulation is interpersonal (handholding) rather than an instructed cognitive/antecedent-focused regulation strategy. Crucially, it fails I10 (no whole-brain group-level voxelwise results reported) and therefore I11 (acceptable whole-brain reporting) is not met. Because E4 is met (ROI-only results), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the report contains only region-of-interest, small-volume-corrected results and between-group interaction contrasts without any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation maps or within-group task effects. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only ROI/SVC results, no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (reports only between-group interactions with no within-group task effect reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images), I8 (sample with patient and control groups reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy reported — task is an interference task superimposed on affective images, not an instructed regulation like reappraisal), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated within-group contrasts reported — only between-group interactions shown), I10 (no whole-brain voxelwise group-level maps reported; all inferences are SVC within ROIs). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study meets the review objective: task-based fMRI with visual emotional stimuli (IAPS and in-house pictures) and reports an unregulated viewing contrast (Negative > Neutral). It provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise results with MNI coordinates and 16 reported peaks (Table tb3). Sample comprises healthy participants. Although no emotion-regulation instruction was given (so I6 is not applicable), the inclusion criteria permit unregulated viewing contrasts (I9). Small-volume correction is mentioned for some inferences but spatial scope is reported as whole-brain and peak coordinates are provided, so this does not trigger exclusion E4. Therefore the study satisfies I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, and I11 and violates no exclusion criteria.

This study reports a task-based fMRI experiment using visual emotional face stimuli and provides whole-brain peak coordinates, but the reported analyses are exclusively between-group interaction contrasts (FHR vs HC for face>shape). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual emotional stimuli), I8 (acceptable sample), I10 (whole-brain, coordinates reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy reported), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation contrast or an unregulated within-group viewing contrast is reported; only between-group interaction maps are provided). Exclusion criteria met: E6 (reports ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect for any group). Therefore the study is excluded.

Exclusion criteria met: E5 (study reports only resting-state/seed-based connectivity analyses with no whole-brain task activation maps) and E6 (reports only between-group contrasts with no within-task task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I8 (sample includes patient and control groups). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not a task-based fMRI study — resting-state), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation task), I7 (no visual emotional stimuli), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts), I10 (no whole-brain task-evoked activation maps with coordinates). Therefore the study does not address the meta-analysis objective and must be excluded.

The study is an fMRI task with visual face stimuli and whole-brain group analyses, and reports within-task affective contrasts, but it does not instruct participants to use an emotion regulation strategy (e.g., cognitive reappraisal or other instructed up-/down-regulation). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: static headshots), I8 (sample qualifies: adolescents), I9 (reports within-task contrasts: acceptance>rejection, interest contrasts), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise group analyses with coordinates), I11 (results clearly described). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no evidence that an emotion regulation strategy was instructed; task involved receiving peer feedback and rating feelings, not instruction to reappraise or otherwise regulate). No exclusion criteria were triggered. Because the review requires all inclusion criteria to be met, the study must be excluded for failing I6.

Excluded under E4: the NeuroStore record indicates all analyses used a region-of-interest spatial scope (ROI) with results reported only within ROIs and no whole-brain, voxelwise group-level activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS and other pictures), I8 (eligible sample: healthy adults), I9 (within-task unregulated viewing contrasts reported: Disgust>Neutral, Fear>Neutral). Inclusion criteria not met: I10 (no whole-brain evidence reported), I6 (no instructed emotion regulation). fulltext_incomplete=false

The study is task-based fMRI with visual emotional face stimuli and an eligible sample (meets I5, I7, I8). However, it does not report an instructed emotion-regulation task or contrasts of instructed regulation (I6 not met), nor does it report within-task emotion regulation or simple unregulated viewing contrasts (I9 not met). All reported analyses are region-of-interest (ROI) and PPI connectivity results with no whole-brain voxelwise task-activation maps or peak coordinates in standard space (I10 not met). Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E4 (reports only ROI/SVC results with no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Conclusion: EXCLUDE.

The paper reports only between-group multivariate decoding contrasts (age-group omnibus comparisons) without any within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast (e.g., emotion > baseline or reappraise > look). Thus it meets exclusion criterion E6 (only between-group contrasts reported). It does meet I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: film clips), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (whole-brain coordinates reported), and I11 (coordinates/tables described). It does not meet I6 (no instructed regulation) and I9 (no within-task regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts). Full text is available in record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation with visual stimuli, healthy adult sample, and reports within-task contrasts and whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results (meets I5, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11). However, participants were not instructed to use any emotion regulation strategy; primes were passively viewed and the design assessed implicit modulation rather than instructed regulation. Thus it does not meet I6 (regulation instruction required). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports a task-based fMRI Affective Picture Viewing Task using visual IAPS stimuli and a within-group unregulated viewing contrast (negative > positive) in a healthy female sample (n=58). The analysis is a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise second-level t-test with FWE-corrected cluster inference and reported MNI peak coordinates. These elements satisfy the review objective (studies that view visual emotional stimuli without regulation) and meet inclusion criteria I5, I7, I8, I9, I10 and I11. No exclusion criteria apply (whole-brain results reported; not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and includes within-group effects). Note: the task did not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met), but the protocol and contrasts align with the review’s allowance for unregulated viewing contrasts (I9).

The study is an fMRI task with visual emotional face stimuli (I5, I7) in an eligible sample (I8) and reports group-level voxelwise results with peak coordinates in MNI space (I10). However, the task assesses automatic resolution of emotional conflict (identify face while ignoring an overlying emotion word) rather than an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (violates I6). The NeuroStore record lists only between-group interaction contrasts (group × trial-type) and a PPI connectivity contrast; no within-group task activation contrast related to instructed regulation or unregulated viewing is reported, so the paper appears to report ONLY between-group contrasts/interactions (meets exclusion E6) and does not meet I6 and I9. Therefore the study is excluded.

Meets all review criteria: (1) Task-based fMRI with an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (affect labeling), (2) Visual emotional stimuli (photographic faces), (3) Within-task contrast directly comparing regulation-related condition (label emotion > match emotion), (4) Group-level whole-brain voxelwise analysis with corrected inference and reported peak coordinates (MNI), (5) Healthy participant sample reported. Although the study also used DCM/effective connectivity, it additionally reports whole-brain task activation so it does not meet exclusion E5. Therefore all required inclusion criteria are satisfied (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10, I11) and no exclusion criteria apply.

(a) Exclusion criteria met: E7 — the task is an instructed empathy/perspective-taking task ("empathize with perceived emotional or neutral faces") with no instruction to amplify or dampen emotional responses, which the review excludes. (b) Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—photographs of faces), I8 (healthy adult sample), I9 (reports within-task contrasts such as 'intentional empathy for familiar angry > baseline'), I10 (whole-brain, voxelwise results with coordinates). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I6 — no emotion regulation strategy (e.g. reappraisal, instructed down-/up-regulation, acceptance, or instructed cognitive control) was instructed. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study (Cyberball social exclusion) using visual stimuli (pictures of virtual players, ball, on-screen phrases) and reports within-task contrasts of social exclusion > inclusion for both groups (patients and controls). Results are whole-brain, voxelwise with peak coordinates in MNI space and appropriate cluster-level inference reported. The study therefore provides the unregulated viewing contrast (emotion induction) that the meta-analysis accepts. Sample and reporting meet criteria for inclusion. Note: the task does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met), but the review accepts studies that involve unregulated viewing contrasts (I9), which this paper provides.

The study instructs voluntary emotion regulation (attentional focusing) during anticipation and reports within-task contrasts, but the regulated emotional stimuli are primarily auditory (aversive sounds) and monetary outcomes rather than visual images, violating the stimulus-visual criterion. In addition, the NeuroStore extraction indicates results are reported with region-of-interest small-volume correction (spatial scope: region of interest; FWE SVC), suggesting no qualifying whole-brain, voxelwise activation map is provided. Therefore the study fails the visual-stimulus inclusion criterion and appears to report only ROI/SVC results (exclusion E4).

This study is excluded because it reports only a between-group omnibus contrast and does not provide any within-group task activation contrasts related to emotion regulation. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (only between-group contrasts reported). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (whole-brain group-level results with peak coordinates), I11 (coordinates reported in table). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy such as reappraisal or similar), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast reported for any group). Based on the NeuroStore record, the listed analysis (omnibus, between-group; whole-brain) and reported peaks do not satisfy the requirement for within-task regulation contrasts, so the study does not meet all inclusion criteria for this review.

Excluded because the study reports only between-group contrasts/interactions and does not present any within-task (within-group) emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrasts. Specifically: exclusion criteria met: E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli: IAPS images), I8 (sample qualifies; patient and control groups reported separately), I10 (at least one group-level whole-brain task map reported with peak coordinates -- Analysis 2), I11 (results reported in tables).
