Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy; task instructed a perceptual response), I9 (no within-task contrasts such as “emotion > neutral” or “reappraise > look” for any group). Because E6 is met (ONLY between-group contrasts with no within-group task effect), the study must be excluded.

Excluded because the study used purely auditory stimuli (audiotaped narrative stories) rather than visual stimuli, failing inclusion criterion I7, and it reports only region-of-interest (ROI) / region-level results with no whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level activation map, meeting exclusion criterion E4 and failing inclusion criterion I10. It does meet several inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (an instructed emotion regulation strategy—distraction), I8 (sample and control group reported), and I9 (reports within-task regulation contrasts such as anger-distraction > anger-engagement). However, because the regulated stimuli are non-visual (I7 not met) and no whole-brain coordinates/map are provided (I10 not met; E4 applies), the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This study is excluded because it does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy (I6 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study using visual face stimuli and reports within-task unregulated viewing habituation contrasts with whole-brain voxelwise peaks in MNI space in an adolescent sample. Specifically: inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (eligible sample), I9 (reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts, e.g., Fear1>Fear2 habituation), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise results with peak coordinates in standard space), I11 (results reported as peaks/tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; task was incidental gender identification). No exclusion criteria appear to be triggered: E3-E7 not applicable (not a review; whole-brain results reported; not connectivity-only; contains within-group task effects; not an empathy/perspective-taking regulation task). Full text is complete as provided.

The study does not instruct participants to engage in an emotion-regulation strategy; the task is a gender-identification facial emotion task (identify male/female), so I6 (instructed emotion regulation) is not met. It does meet other inclusion criteria: task-based fMRI (I5); visual stimuli (I7); sample acceptable (I8); reports an unregulated viewing contrast Angry>Neutral (I9); provides whole-brain, corrected group-level results with reported peaks (I10, I11). No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore excluded because I6 is not satisfied.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using instructed cognitive distraction during anticipation as an emotion-regulation strategy (I6). Emotional stimuli are visual IAPS pictures (I7). Participants are healthy humans with reported sample details (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation and unregulated viewing (negative > neutral; interaction of working memory load and emotion anticipation) (I9). Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with MNI coordinates and FWE correction are reported (I10,I11). Although one interaction analysis used small-volume correction for the amygdala, the paper also reports whole-brain voxelwise results, so it is not excluded under ROI-only reporting. Therefore the study should be included for the meta-analysis of instructed regulation of visual emotional stimuli.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion-regulation strategy (attentional deployment: focus on collected gains vs missed chances) (I6). The regulated stimuli are visual (arrays of boxes, highlighted outcome regions and text) (I7). Participant sample is reported (n=18) and acceptable (I8). The paper reports within-task contrasts directly related to regulation (GF > MF and related contrasts) (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise with reported peak coordinates in MNI space and FWE-corrected inference (I10,I11). No exclusion criteria are met: the study is empirical, reports whole-brain task activation contrasts (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, or between-group-only), and is not an empathy-only perspective-taking task. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study does not meet the review's definition of an instructed emotion-regulation task (I6) and does not report a within-task emotion-regulation contrast (I9). The task required approach/avoidance joystick movements in response to facial expressions and examined incongruent vs congruent action mappings; this is voluntary control over action tendencies but not an instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance or explicit instructions to amplify/dampen emotional responses. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (whole-brain group-level analyses reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy), I9 (no within-task regulation contrast like reappraise>look or similar). Exclusion criteria met: none (no E3–E7 applicable).

Exclusion E4 applies: the reported analysis is region-of-interest only (frontal Stroop ROIs) with no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked map. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI: Stroop Color-Word Task) and I8 (sample qualifies: healthy participants). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation strategy reported), I7 (stimuli are color words, not emotional visual stimuli), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or unregulated viewing contrast reported; analysis is a cross-subject regression relating neural Stroop response to stress-related working memory), I10 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise map with peak coordinates), I11 (not applicable because no whole-brain results reported in text/tables/figures). Conclusion: Exclude because the study does not address emotion regulation with emotional visual stimuli and reports only ROI results (E4).

The study reports task-based fMRI (I5) using visual stimuli (20-second video clips; own-child and unfamiliar-child) satisfying I7. It reports within-task, unregulated viewing contrasts (Own Positive > Stranger Positive; Own Negative > Stranger Negative), meeting I9. Results are whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates in Talairach and cluster-level correction, satisfying I10 and I11. The sample (clinical mothers with depressive disorder) is an eligible participant group (I8). Although no emotion-regulation instructions are reported (I6 not applicable), the meta-analysis objective explicitly includes studies that view emotional stimuli without regulating; thus lack of regulation instruction does not exclude the study. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E4), not connectivity-only (E5), not only between-group contrasts (E6), and not a non-empirical paper (E3). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion as an unregulated viewing task with whole-brain activation contrasts.

Excluded because the study does not meet the requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation task. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli — film clips), I8 (sample acceptable), I10 (whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I11 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy such as reappraisal/acceptance instruction — ‘accept’ here is an economic decision, not an instructed regulation condition), I9 (no within-task contrast that tests an instructed emotion-regulation condition, e.g., reappraise > look). No exclusion criteria from the review were triggered (none of E3–E7 apply). Therefore the study is excluded because it fails to satisfy I6 and I9.

The study is a task-based fMRI experiment (Think/No-Think) that instructs participants to suppress (No-Think) or retrieve (Think) unpleasant images, satisfying the requirement for an instructed emotion-regulation/cognitive-control strategy. Stimuli are visual (IAPS scenes). The sample (n=22 healthy adults) meets the sample inclusion. The paper reports within-task contrasts relevant to regulation (No-Think > Think and Think > No-Think). Crucially, it includes group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with FWE-corrected peak coordinates (Table t2), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (results are not ROI-only, not only connectivity, not non-empirical, not empathy/perspective-taking only, and include within-group task effects). Therefore all inclusion criteria I5–I11 are met and the study should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study using visual stimuli (silent video clips of children) with an unregulated viewing contrast (separation > play) that was correlated with BDNF methylation. It reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level results with peak coordinates in MNI and corrected inference (Monte Carlo cluster correction). The sample (n=46 mothers, including an interpersonal violence-related PTSD group) is an eligible participant group. Although the task did not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (criterion I6 not met), the review objective explicitly allows studies that involve viewing without regulating, and the paper provides an appropriate within-task unregulated viewing contrast (I9). Therefore the study meets the required inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis.

This study does not instruct an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met): the task is the Ultimatum Game with accept/reject decisions, and the record contains no indication that participants were instructed to reappraise, distance, accept as a regulation strategy, or otherwise regulate their emotional responses. Whole-brain evidence is not clearly reported (I10 not met): the only explicitly described analysis is a region-of-interest analysis (right cerebellum); NeuroStore entries for other analyses list reported peaks but provide no clear whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli), I8 (sample qualifies), I9 (within-task contrast present: fair > unfair). No exclusion criteria clearly apply (none met). Therefore exclude because key inclusion criteria I6 and I10 are not satisfied, despite meeting other inclusions.

This study reports an implicit emotional face-processing task (incidental labeling) with no instruction to regulate emotion (participants were not instructed to be mindful or to use any regulation strategy). It therefore fails the required inclusion criterion I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy). It does meet other inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI), I7 (visual stimuli—faces), I8 (sample acceptable), I9 (reports unregulated viewing contrasts such as emotion > fixation and affect > gender), I10 (reports whole-brain group-level analyses with peak coordinates), and I11 (results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., the study includes whole-brain maps, not only ROI or connectivity). Thus exclude due to unmet I6.

This study is a task-based fMRI investigation of instructed positive emotion upregulation using visual IAPS images in a sample including MDD patients and healthy controls, so it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7 and I8. However, the NeuroStore record only reports seed-based gPPI connectivity results (a between-group interaction contrast: CON Increase > MDD View) that are whole-brain connectivity maps; it does not report any within-task activation contrasts for any group nor any whole-brain task activation (voxelwise activation) maps. Therefore it violates exclusion criteria E5 (reports only seed-based/effective connectivity without accompanying whole-brain task activation maps) and E6 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions with no within-group task effect). Inclusion criteria I9 (within-task contrasts) and I10 (whole-brain task-evoked activation map with peak coordinates) are not met. Full text appears complete in this record. Exclusion IDs met: E5, E6. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I6, I7, I8. Inclusion IDs not met: I9, I10.

This study meets all required inclusion criteria for the review: it is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using an instructed emotion regulation paradigm (enhance/suppress/attend; cognitive reappraisal-type instructions) (I6); stimuli are visual IAPS images (I7); the sample includes a clinical group with results reported for within-group analyses (I8); the paper reports within-task contrasts/associations related to regulation (e.g. sustained 2nd half > 1st half within-group regressions) (I9); and it includes whole-brain, group-level voxelwise maps with peak coordinates and multiple-comparison correction (Analyses 3 and 4) (I10), reported in tables (I11). No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply: the paper is empirical, includes whole-brain activation results (not only ROI or connectivity), and reports within-group task effects. Therefore the article should be included.

This study is excluded because it does not address instructed emotion regulation of visual emotional stimuli and reports only ROI/between-group results. Inclusion: I5 (task-based fMRI) is met. Not met: I6 (no instructed emotion regulation; task is a cognitive Go/No-Go with letter stimuli), I7 (stimuli are non-emotional letters, not visual emotional images/clips), I9 (no within-task emotion-regulation or viewing contrasts reported), I10 (no whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked map reported). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only region-of-interest result reported for bilateral sgACC, no whole-brain analysis) and E6 (only a between-group/omnibus diagnosis contrast shown; no within-group task effect reported). Full text is available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets the review objective and the relevant inclusion criteria. It is a task-based fMRI study (I5) using visual threat/safe cues (I7). Participants include patient and healthy control groups reported separately (I8). The paper reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (e.g. shock > safe, safe > shock) suitable for inclusion as unregulated viewing contrasts (I9). Analyses are whole-brain, voxelwise with peak coordinates in standard (MNI) space reported in tables (I10, I11). The task involves anticipatory threat but does not instruct an emotion regulation strategy, so I6 (instruction to regulate) is not met; however the meta-analysis objective accepts unregulated viewing contrasts. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-empirical, or empathy-perspective tasks; and within-group task effects are reported, so E4–E7 do not apply). Therefore the study is eligible for inclusion.

Exclusion because the study does not instruct participants to use an emotion-regulation strategy (I6 not met). It is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual stimuli (I7), includes an eligible sample (I8), reports within-task unregulated viewing contrasts (bodies>scrambled, faces>scrambled) (I9), provides whole-brain group-level maps with MNI coordinates (I10) and acceptable reporting (I11). No exclusion criteria were met (none of E3–E7 apply).

The study is excluded because it does not report an instructed emotion regulation task (I6 not met) and does not present any within-task contrast related to emotion regulation or unregulated viewing (I9 not met). The NeuroStore record shows only between-group omnibus/interaction contrasts and PPI connectivity analyses, consistent with exclusion criterion E6 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported with no within-group task effect). The record does confirm it is a task-based fMRI study (I5), uses visual stimuli (photograph of proposer) (I7), has an eligible sample (I8), and reports whole-brain voxelwise analyses with peak coordinates (I10, I11).

Excluded because the study does not meet key inclusion criteria and meets an exclusion criterion. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (the NeuroStore record reports only between-group interaction contrasts [LTM vs MNP for SC>NT and SP>NT] with no within-group task activation contrasts presented). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I8 (sample qualifies: healthy participants of eligible ages), I10 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results reported with coordinates in MNI), I11 (results reported in tables/coordinates). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no instructed emotion-regulation strategy reported; task is self-referential judgment with no regulation instruction), I7 (stimuli are adjectives/words — word stimuli are excluded by I7), I9 (no within-task unregulated viewing contrast reported for any group; reported contrasts are only between-group interactions). Given these violations, the study must be excluded from the review.
